title.en: Volume 323 Biographies 211: Foreign States 4: Ryūkyū Islands, Luzon, Camarines Sur, Maluku Islands, Mindanao, Dapitan, Keelung, Borneo, Belitung Island, Gumalalang, Pangasinan, Banjarmasin
title.raw: 卷三百二十三 列傳第二百十一 外國四 琉球 呂宋 合貓里 美洛居 沙瑤吶嗶嘽 雞籠 婆羅 麻葉甕 古麻喇朗 馮嘉施蘭 文郎馬神 Volume 323 Biographies 211: Foreign States 4: Ryūkyū Islands, Luzon, Camarines Sur, Maluku Islands, Mindanao, Dapitan, Keelung, Borneo, Belitung Island, Gumalalang, Pangasinan, Banjarmasin

sentences.zh: 琉球居東南大海中，自古不通中國。

translations.literal: Ryūkyū lay in the great sea to the southeast; from antiquity it had no intercourse with China.
translations.idiomatic: The Ryūkyū Islands lay far out in the southeastern sea and had had no contact with China since ancient times.

sentences.zh: 元世祖遣官招諭之，不能達。

translations.literal: The Yuan Shizu emperor sent officials to summon and instruct them, but could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan sent envoys to summon them, but the mission never reached the islands.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，其國有三王，曰中山，曰山南，曰山北，皆以尚為姓，而中山最強。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, their state had three kings, called Zhongshan, Shannan, and Shanbei; all bore the surname Shang, and Zhongshan was strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign the realm was divided among three kings—of Zhongshan, Shannan, and Shanbei—all of the Shang clan, with Zhongshan the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 五年正月命行人楊載以即位建元詔告其國，其中山王察度遣弟泰期等隨載入朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he ordered the credential bearer Yang Zai to announce the accession and establishment of the era to their state; King Chadu of Zhongshan sent his younger brother Taiqi and others to follow Zai to court and present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year the emperor sent the envoy Yang Zai to announce his accession and new reign title; King Chadu of Zhongshan sent his brother Taiqi and others to accompany Zai to court with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，賜《大統歷》及文綺、紗羅有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed the 《Great Unity Calendar》 and patterned silks and gauzes in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded them with the 《Great Unity Calendar》 and graded gifts of brocade and gauze.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，泰期復來貢，並上皇太子箋。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Taiqi came again with tribute and also submitted a memorial to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year Taiqi returned with tribute and presented a memorial to the crown prince as well.

sentences.zh: 命刑部侍郎李浩齎賜文綺、陶鐵器，且以陶器七萬、鐵器千，就其國市馬。

translations.literal: Li Hao, vice minister of justice, was ordered to carry patterned silks and ceramic and iron goods as gifts, and also to take seventy thousand pieces of pottery and a thousand iron implements to purchase horses in their state.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of justice Li Hao was sent with brocades and ceramic and iron wares as gifts, and with seventy thousand pottery pieces and a thousand iron implements to buy horses in Ryūkyū.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，泰期隨浩入貢，得馬四十匹。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year Taiqi followed Hao in presenting tribute; forty horses were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the ninth year Taiqi accompanied Hao to court with tribute, having secured forty horses.

sentences.zh: 浩言其國不貴紈綺，惟貴磁器、鐵釜，自是賞賚多用諸物。

translations.literal: Hao reported that their state did not value fine silks but prized only porcelain and iron cauldrons; from then on rewards and gifts mostly used these items.
translations.idiomatic: Hao reported that the islanders cared little for fine silks but valued porcelain and iron pots; thereafter imperial gifts to them were chiefly of those goods.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使賀正旦，貢馬十六匹、硫黃千斤。

translations.literal: The next year they sent envoys to congratulate the New Year and presented sixteen horses and a thousand jin of sulfur.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent envoys for the New Year audience with sixteen horses and a thousand jin of sulfur as tribute.

sentences.zh: 又明年復貢。

translations.literal: The year after that they presented tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again the year after that.

sentences.zh: 山南王承察度亦遣使朝貢，禮賜如中山。

translations.literal: King Chengchadu of Shannan also sent envoys to court with tribute; ritual gifts were the same as for Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: King Chengchadu of Shannan also sent envoys with tribute, and received the same ceremonial rewards as Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，中山來貢，遣內官送其使還國。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year Zhongshan came with tribute; an inner palace official was sent to escort their envoys home.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year Zhongshan sent tribute, and an imperial eunuch was dispatched to escort the envoys home.

sentences.zh: 明年與山南王並來貢，詔賜二王鍍金銀印。

translations.literal: The next year they came with Shannan to present tribute together; an edict bestowed on the two kings gilded gold-and-silver seals.
translations.idiomatic: The next year both kings sent tribute together, and the court granted each a gilded gold-and-silver seal.

sentences.zh: 時二王與山北王爭雄，互相攻伐。

translations.literal: At that time the two kings and the king of Shanbei contended for supremacy and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the two southern kings and the king of Shanbei were vying for power and raiding one another.

sentences.zh: 命內史監丞梁民賜之敕，令罷兵息民，三王並奉命。

translations.literal: Liang Min, assistant director of the Secretariat, was ordered to bestow an imperial letter on them, commanding them to cease arms and give the people rest; all three kings obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liang Min of the Secretariat with an imperial letter ordering them to lay down arms and spare their people; all three kings complied.

sentences.zh: 山北王怕尼芝即遣使偕二王使朝貢。

translations.literal: King Panizhi of Shanbei then sent envoys together with the envoys of the two kings to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Panizhi of Shanbei then sent envoys to court alongside those of the other two kings.

sentences.zh: 十八年又貢，賜山北王鍍金銀印如二王，而賜二王海舟各一。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year they presented tribute again; the king of Shanbei was given a gilded gold-and-silver seal like the two kings, while each of the two kings was given one seagoing vessel.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the eighteenth year; Shanbei received a gilded seal like the other two kings, and each of the southern kings was given a seagoing vessel.

sentences.zh: 自是，三王屢遣使奉貢，中山王尤數。

translations.literal: From then on the three kings repeatedly sent envoys with tribute; the king of Zhongshan did so especially often.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all three kings sent tribute repeatedly, Zhongshan most frequently of all.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，中山來貢，其通事私攜乳香十斤、胡椒三百斤入都，為門者所獲，當入官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Zhongshan came with tribute; their interpreter privately carried ten jin of frankincense and three hundred jin of pepper into the capital, was seized by gate guards, and the goods were due for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Zhongshan sent tribute; their interpreter had smuggled ten jin of frankincense and three hundred jin of pepper into the capital, was caught at the gate, and the goods were to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔還之，仍賜以鈔。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the goods returned and paper money was still bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the goods returned and still gave him paper money as a gift.

sentences.zh: 二十五年夏，中山貢使以其王從子及寨官子偕來，請肄業國學。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-fifth year the tribute envoys of Zhongshan brought the king's nephew and sons of fortress officials, asking to study at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-fifth year Zhongshan's envoys brought the king's nephew and sons of local officials, asking that they be enrolled at the National University.

sentences.zh: 從之，賜衣巾靴襪並夏衣一襲。

translations.literal: The request was granted; they were given caps, robes, boots, and socks, and one set of summer garments.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and they were given caps, gowns, boots, socks, and a set of summer clothes.

sentences.zh: 其冬，山南王亦遣從子及寨官子入國學，賜賚如之。

translations.literal: That winter the king of Shannan also sent his nephew and sons of fortress officials to the National University; gifts were the same.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Shannan also sent his nephew and sons of local officials to study at the university, with the same grants of clothing.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲賜冬夏衣以為常。

translations.literal: From then on winter and summer clothing was granted yearly as a fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter annual grants of winter and summer clothing became the rule.

sentences.zh: 明年，中山兩入貢，又遣寨官子肄業國學。

translations.literal: The next year Zhongshan presented tribute twice and again sent sons of fortress officials to study at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhongshan sent tribute twice and again dispatched sons of local officials to study at the university.

sentences.zh: 是時，國法嚴，中山生與山南生有非議詔書者。

translations.literal: At that time state law was strict; students from Zhongshan and Shannan spoke irreverently of an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the law was strict; students from Zhongshan and Shannan were found to have spoken disrespectfully of an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，置之死，而待其國如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he had them put to death, yet treated their states as before.
translations.idiomatic: On learning of it the emperor had them executed, but continued to treat their countries as before.

sentences.zh: 山北王怕尼芝已卒，其嗣王攀安知二十九年春遣使來貢。

translations.literal: King Panizhi of Shanbei had already died; his successor King Pan Anzhi in the spring of the twenty-ninth year sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Panizhi of Shanbei had died; his successor Pan Anzhi sent envoys with tribute in the spring of the twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 令山南生肄國學者歸省，其冬復來。

translations.literal: Students from Shannan studying at the National University were ordered home on leave; that winter they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan students at the university were allowed to return home; they came back the following winter.

sentences.zh: 中山亦遣寨官子二人及女官生姑、魯妹二人，先後來肄業，其感慕華風如此。

translations.literal: Zhongshan also sent two sons of fortress officials and two female students, Gu and Lumai, who came in succession to study; such was their admiration for Chinese culture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan also sent two sons of local officials and two female students, Gu and Lumai, who arrived in turn to study—such was their admiration for Chinese civilization.

sentences.zh: 中山又遣使請賜冠帶，命禮部繪圖，令自制。

translations.literal: Zhongshan again sent envoys requesting bestowal of caps and belts; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to draw pictures so they could make them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan again asked for court caps and belts; the Ministry of Rites was told to supply designs so they could make their own.

sentences.zh: 其王固以請，乃賜之，並賜其臣下冠服。

translations.literal: The king pressed the request firmly, whereupon they were bestowed, and court dress was also given to his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the king pressed the request again, the court granted them, along with official robes for his ministers.

sentences.zh: 又嘉其修職勤，賜閩中舟工三十六戶，以便貢使往來。

translations.literal: Further, in praise of his diligent fulfillment of duty, thirty-six households of Fujian shipwrights were granted to facilitate the coming and going of tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The court also rewarded his diligence by assigning thirty-six Fujian shipwright families to his service, to ease the passage of tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝嗣位，遣官以登極詔諭其國，三王亦奉貢不絕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, officials were sent with an accession edict to instruct their state; the three kings also continued presenting tribute without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui came to the throne, envoys announced his accession to Ryūkyū, and all three kings continued sending tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 成祖承大統，詔諭如前。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu received the great succession; an edict instructed them as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle emperor took the throne, he sent the same kind of accession notice as before.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年春，三王並來貢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yongle all three kings came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first Yongle year all three kings sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 山北王請賜冠帶，詔給賜如中山。

translations.literal: The king of Shanbei requested bestowal of caps and belts; an edict granted them as to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shanbei asked for caps and belts; the court granted them on the same terms as Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 命行人邊信、劉亢齎敕使三國，賜以絨錦、文綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: The credential bearers Bian Xin and Liu Kang were ordered to carry an imperial letter to the three states and bestow velvet brocade, patterned silks, and gauzes.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys Bian Xin and Liu Kang were sent with an imperial letter to all three realms, bearing velvet brocades, figured silks, and gauzes.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，中山王世子武寧遣使告父喪，命禮部遣官諭祭，賻以布帛，遂命武寧襲位。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year the heir of Zhongshan, Wuning, sent envoys to announce his father's death; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to send officials to perform condolence rites, silk cloth was given as funeral gifts, and Wuning was then ordered to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month Zhongshan's heir Wuning announced his father's death; the Ministry of Rites sent officials for the mourning rites and funeral gifts of silk, and Wuning was confirmed as king.

sentences.zh: 四月，山南王從弟汪應祖亦遣使告承察度之喪，謂前王無子，傳位應祖，乞加朝命，且賜冠帶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the king of Shannan's younger cousin Wang Yingzu also sent envoys to announce Chengchadu's death, saying the former king had no son and the throne had passed to Yingzu; he begged imperial confirmation and also caps and belts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Shannan's king sent word that Chengchadu had died without an heir and that his cousin Wang Yingzu had succeeded, asking for imperial recognition and the grant of caps and belts.

sentences.zh: 帝並從之，遂遣官冊封。

translations.literal: The emperor granted both requests and then sent officials to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed to both requests and sent officials to perform the investiture.

sentences.zh: 時山南使臣私齎白金詣處州市磁器，事發，當諭罪。

translations.literal: At that time a Shannan envoy privately carried white gold to Chuzhou to buy porcelain; when the matter came to light he was due for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A Shannan envoy was then found to have smuggled silver to Chuzhou to buy porcelain; when discovered he was liable for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遠方之人，知求利而已，安知禁令。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "People from distant regions know only to seek profit—how would they know prohibitions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Men from afar know only to seek gain—how could they know our prohibitions."

sentences.zh: 悉貰之。

translations.literal: All were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 三年，山南遣寨官子入國學。

translations.literal: In the third year Shannan sent sons of fortress officials to the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shannan sent sons of local officials to the National University.

sentences.zh: 明年，中山亦遣寨官子六人入國學，並獻奄豎數人。

translations.literal: The next year Zhongshan also sent six sons of fortress officials to the National University and presented several castrated youths.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhongshan sent six sons of local officials to the university and also offered several eunuch youths.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼亦人子，無罪刑之，何忍？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "They too are men's sons—how can one punish them without crime? How could one bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They too are someone's children—how can we punish them when they are innocent? How could I bear that?"

sentences.zh: 命禮部還之。

translations.literal: He ordered the Ministry of Rites to return them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Ministry of Rites to send them home.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「還之，慮阻歸化之心，請但賜敕，止其再進。」

translations.literal: A ministry official said: "If they are returned, one fears blocking the mind of coming to allegiance; we ask only to bestow an edict forbidding further presentation."
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials argued that returning them might discourage their desire to submit, and asked only to issue an edict forbidding such gifts in future."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諭以空言，不若示以實事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To instruct with empty words is not as good as showing them a concrete act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Empty words will not teach them as well as a concrete example.

sentences.zh: 今不遣還，彼欲獻媚，必將繼進。

translations.literal: If they are not sent back now, when those people wish to curry favor they will surely continue presenting them.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not send them back, they will surely keep sending more to please us.

sentences.zh: 天地以生物為心，帝王乃可絕人類乎？」

translations.literal: Heaven and earth take nurturing life as their heart—how could an emperor cut off humankind?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth exist to nurture life—how could an emperor destroy human beings?"

sentences.zh: 竟還之。

translations.literal: In the end they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he had them sent home.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，中山王世子思紹遣使告父喪，諭祭，賜賻冊封如前儀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year the heir of Zhongshan, Sishao, sent envoys to announce his father's death; condolence rites were instructed, funeral gifts and investiture were bestowed as in the former ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year Zhongshan's heir Sishao announced his father's death; the court performed the mourning rites and investiture as before.

sentences.zh: 八年，山南遣官生三人入國學，賜巾服靴絛、衾褥帷帳，已復頻有所賜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Shannan sent three official students to the National University; caps, robes, boots, and sashes, quilts, bedding, and curtains were bestowed, and thereafter gifts were frequently given again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Shannan sent three students to the university; they were given caps, gowns, boots, bedding, and curtains, and such gifts were repeated often thereafter.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝與群臣語及之。

translations.literal: One day the emperor spoke of this with his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor mentioned this to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書呂震曰：「昔唐太宗興庠序，新羅、百濟並遣子來學。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Lü Zhen said: "Formerly Emperor Taizong of Tang raised schools; Silla and Baekje both sent sons to study.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of rites Lü Zhen said, "When Emperor Taizong of Tang founded the schools, Silla and Baekje both sent princes to study.

sentences.zh: 爾時僅給廩餼，未若今日賜予之周也。」

translations.literal: At that time they were only given grain stipends—not as comprehensive as today's bestowals."
translations.idiomatic: In those days they received only grain stipends—nothing like the generous grants of today."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠻夷子弟慕義而來，必衣食常充，然後向學。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sons of barbarians come admiring righteousness; their food and clothing must always be ample before they can turn to study.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "These young men from abroad come drawn by our civilization; they must be well fed and clothed before they can devote themselves to learning.

sentences.zh: 此我太祖美意，朕安得違之。」

translations.literal: This was the fine intention of our Taizu—how could I go against it."
translations.idiomatic: That was my ancestor's wise policy, and I cannot depart from it."

sentences.zh: 明年，中山遣國相子及寨官子入國學，因言：「右長史王茂輔翼有年，請擢為國相。

translations.literal: The next year Zhongshan sent the son of the state counselor and sons of fortress officials to the National University, and also reported: "The right chief secretary Wang Mao has assisted for many years—please promote him to state counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhongshan sent the state counselor's son and sons of local officials to the university, reporting that the right chief secretary Wang Mao had served faithfully for years and should be made state counselor.

sentences.zh: 左長史硃復，本江西饒州人，輔臣祖察度四十餘年不懈。

translations.literal: The left chief secretary Zhu Fu was originally a man of Raozhou in Jiangxi; he assisted King Chadu for more than forty years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: The left chief secretary Zhu Fu, a native of Raozhou in Jiangxi, had served King Chadu's house for more than forty years without faltering.

sentences.zh: 今年逾八十，請令致仕還鄉。」

translations.literal: This year he is over eighty; we ask that he be allowed to retire and return home."
translations.idiomatic: He is now over eighty, and we ask that he be permitted to retire and return home."

sentences.zh: 從之，乃命復、茂並為國相，復兼左長史致仕，茂兼右長史任其國事。

translations.literal: The request was granted; Fu and Mao were both appointed state counselors, Fu also left chief secretary with retirement, and Mao also right chief secretary to handle their state's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted: Fu and Mao were both made state counselors; Fu retired as left chief secretary, and Mao took up the right chief secretary post to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，中山遣寨官子十三人入國學。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Zhongshan sent thirteen sons of fortress officials to the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Zhongshan sent thirteen sons of local officials to the National University.

sentences.zh: 時山南王應祖為其兄達勃期所弒，諸寨官討誅之，推應祖子他魯每為主，以十三年三月請封。

translations.literal: At that time King Yingzu of Shannan was murdered by his elder brother Daboqi; the fortress officials punished and executed him and set up Yingzu's son Tarumei as ruler; in the third month of the thirteenth year they requested investiture.
translations.idiomatic: King Yingzu of Shannan had been murdered by his brother Daboqi; local leaders put the assassin to death and set up Yingzu's son Tarumei as king, requesting investiture in the third month of the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 命行人陳季若等封為山南王，賜誥命冠服及寶鈔萬五千錠。

translations.literal: The credential bearer Chen Jiruo and others were ordered to invest him as king of Shannan and bestow patent, investiture robes, and fifteen thousand ingots of treasure notes.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiruo and other envoys were sent to invest Tarumei as king of Shannan, with patent, robes, and fifteen thousand ingots of treasure notes.

sentences.zh: 琉球之分三王也，惟山北最弱，故其朝貢亦最稀。

translations.literal: When Ryūkyū was divided among three kings, only Shanbei was weakest, so its court tribute was also most infrequent.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three Ryūkyū kingdoms Shanbei was the weakest, and its tribute missions were the rarest.

sentences.zh: 自永樂三年入貢後，至是年四月始入貢。

translations.literal: After presenting tribute in the third year of Yongle, it was not until the fourth month of this year that tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: After sending tribute in Yongle 3, Shanbei sent none again until the fourth month of this year.

sentences.zh: 其後，竟為二王所並，而中山益強，以其國富，一歲常再貢三貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was in the end absorbed by the two kings, while Zhongshan grew stronger; because its state was wealthy, in one year it often presented tribute twice or thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Shanbei was eventually absorbed by the other two kingdoms, while Zhongshan grew ever stronger; its wealth allowed it to send tribute two or three times a year.

sentences.zh: 天朝雖厭其繁，不能卻也。

translations.literal: Although the celestial court grew weary of the frequency, it could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: The court found the frequency burdensome but could not turn the missions away.

sentences.zh: 其冬，貢使還，至福建，擅奪海舶，殺官軍，且毆傷中官，掠其衣物。

translations.literal: That winter, as the tribute envoys returned and reached Fujian, they seized seagoing vessels without authority, killed government troops, and also beat and injured eunuch officials and plundered their clothing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the return journey through Fujian, the envoys seized merchant ships, killed government troops, assaulted imperial eunuchs, and robbed their belongings.

sentences.zh: 事聞，戮其為首者，余六十七人付其主自治。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the ringleaders were executed; the remaining sixty-seven were handed to their king for his own punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court the ringleaders were executed; the other sixty-seven were handed back to their king for punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使謝罪，帝待之如初，其修貢益謹。

translations.literal: The next year they sent envoys to apologize; the emperor treated them as at first, and their presentation of tribute became even more careful.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent envoys to apologize; the emperor treated them as before, and their tribute missions became even more punctilious.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，中山王世子尚巴志來告父喪，諭祭賜賻如常儀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the heir of Zhongshan, Shang Bazhi, came to announce his father's death; condolence rites and funeral gifts were instructed as in the usual ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year Zhongshan's heir Shang Bazhi announced his father's death; the court performed the usual mourning rites and funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，命行人方彝詔告其國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong succeeded to the throne, the credential bearer Fang Yi was ordered to announce it to their state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, the envoy Fang Yi was sent to announce his accession to Ryūkyū.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年命中官齎敕封巴志為中山王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi an inner palace official was ordered to carry an imperial letter investing Bazhi as king of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Hongxi year an imperial eunuch was sent to invest Bazhi as king of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，其王以冠服未給，遣使來請，命制皮弁服賜之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, because court dress had not been given, the king sent envoys to request it; leather cap-and-gown dress was ordered made and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 the king, having received no court dress, sent envoys to request it; the court had leather cap-and-gown robes made and sent to him.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，帝以中山王朝貢彌謹，遣官齎敕往勞，賜羅錦諸物。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, because Zhongshan's court tribute was ever more careful, the emperor sent officials with an imperial letter to express appreciation and bestowed gauze brocades and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xuande 3, noting Zhongshan's ever more diligent tribute, the emperor sent officials with a letter of commendation and gifts of gauze brocades.

sentences.zh: 山南自四年兩貢，終帝世不復至，亦為中山所並矣。

translations.literal: Shannan presented tribute twice from the fourth year onward and never came again through the end of the emperor's reign; it too was absorbed by Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan sent tribute twice in the fourth year and never again during that reign; it too had been absorbed by Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 自是，惟中山一國朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: From then on only the one state of Zhongshan presented court tribute without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter only Zhongshan continued sending tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，其使者言：「初入閩時，止具貢物報聞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong their envoys said: "When we first entered Fujian we reported only the tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 their envoys reported that on entering Fujian they had declared only their tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 下人所齎海、螺殼，失於開報，悉為官司所沒入，致來往乏資，乞賜垂憫。」

translations.literal: The cowries and shells carried by subordinates were omitted from the declaration and were all confiscated by officials, causing our coming and going to lack funds—we beg compassionate consideration."
translations.idiomatic: Cowries and shells carried by their attendants had not been declared and were all confiscated, leaving them without funds for the journey; they begged the court's compassion."

sentences.zh: 命給直如例。

translations.literal: They were ordered payment at the standard rate.
translations.idiomatic: They were paid compensation according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 明年，貢使至浙江，典市舶者復請籍其所齎，帝曰：「番人以貿易為利，此二物取之何用，其悉還之，著為令。」

translations.literal: The next year, when tribute envoys reached Zhejiang, the maritime trade commissioner again asked to register what they carried; the emperor said: "Barbarians take trade as profit—what use is there in taking these two kinds of goods? Return them all and make this a standing order."
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the envoys reached Zhejiang, the maritime trade officials again tried to register their goods; the emperor said, "These foreigners live by trade—what use are cowries and shells to us? Return everything and make that the rule."

sentences.zh: 使者奏：「本國陪臣冠服，皆國初所賜，歲久敝壞，乞再給。」

translations.literal: The envoys memorialized: "The caps and robes of our state's attending ministers were all bestowed at the founding of the state; after many years they are worn out—we beg they be given again."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys also asked that court robes for their ministers, originally granted at the dynasty's founding and now worn out, be renewed."

sentences.zh: 又言：「小邦遵奉正朔，海道險遠，受歷之使，或半歲一歲始返，常懼後時。」

translations.literal: They also said: "Our small state observes the correct calendar; the sea route is perilous and far, and envoys receiving the calendar sometimes only return after half a year or a year—we constantly fear being late."
translations.idiomatic: They also noted that their remote island followed the Chinese calendar, but envoys carrying the annual calendar sometimes took half a year or more to return, and they feared being late."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「冠服令本邦自制。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For caps and robes, order your own state to make them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that they should make their own court dress.

sentences.zh: 《大統歷》，福建布政司給予之。」

translations.literal: The 《Great Unity Calendar》 shall be supplied by the Fujian provincial administration commission."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Great Unity Calendar》 would be issued by the Fujian provincial administration."

sentences.zh: 七年正月，中山世子尚忠來告父喪，命給事中余忭、行人劉遜封忠為中山王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year the heir of Zhongshan, Shang Zhong, came to announce his father's death; the supervising secretary Yu Min and the credential bearer Liu Xun were ordered to invest Zhong as king of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Zhongshan's heir Shang Zhong announced his father's death; Yu Min and Liu Xun were sent to invest him as king.

sentences.zh: 敕使之用給事中，自茲始也。

translations.literal: The use of supervising secretaries as imperial messengers began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of sending supervising secretaries as imperial envoys began with this mission.

sentences.zh: 忭等還，受其黃金、沉香、倭扇之贈，為偵事者所覺，並下吏，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: When Yu Min and the others returned they accepted gifts of gold, aloeswood, and Japanese fans; spies detected it and they were all handed to the law officers, flogged, and released.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Yu Min and his party accepted gifts of gold, aloeswood, and Japanese fans; informers exposed them, and all were arrested, flogged, and released.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，世子尚思達來告父喪，命給事中陳傅、行人萬祥往封。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year the heir Shang Sida came to announce his father's death; the supervising secretary Chen Fu and the credential bearer Wan Xiang were ordered to go and invest him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year the heir Shang Sida announced his father's death; Chen Fu and Wan Xiang were sent to perform the investiture.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，思達卒，無子，其叔父金福攝國事，遣使告喪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai Sida died without a son; his uncle Jin Fu took charge of state affairs and sent envoys to announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 2 Sida died childless; his uncle Jin Fu assumed regency and sent envoys to announce the death.

sentences.zh: 命給事中喬毅、行人童守宏封金福為王。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Qiao Yi and the credential bearer Tong Shouhong were ordered to invest Jin Fu as king.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yi and Tong Shouhong were sent to invest Jin Fu as king.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，金福弟泰久奏：「長兄金福殂，次兄布里與兄子志魯爭立，兩傷俱殞，所賜印亦毀壞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year Jin Fu's younger brother Taijiu memorialized: "The eldest brother Jin Fu has died; the second brother Buri and the elder brother's son Zhilu contended for the throne, both were wounded and perished, and the bestowed seal was also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year Jin Fu's brother Taijiu reported that the eldest brother had died, that the second brother Buri and the nephew Zhilu had fought over the succession and both been killed, and that the imperial seal had been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 國中臣民推臣權攝國事，乞再賜印鎮撫遠籓。」

translations.literal: The ministers and people of the state have pushed me to take charge of affairs temporarily; we beg a seal be bestowed again to pacify the distant frontier."
translations.idiomatic: The nobles and people had asked him to govern provisionally and begged for a new seal to govern the distant realm."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年四月命給事中嚴誠、行人劉儉封泰久為王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year the supervising secretary Yan Cheng and the credential bearer Liu Jian were ordered to invest Taijiu as king.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month Yan Cheng and Liu Jian were sent to invest Taijiu as king.

sentences.zh: 天順六年三月，世子尚德來告父喪，命給事中潘榮、行人蔡哲封為王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Tianshun, the heir Shang De came to announce his father's death; the supervising secretary Pan Rong and the credential bearer Cai Zhe were ordered to invest him as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianshun 6 the heir Shang De reported his father's death, and Pan Rong and Cai Zhe were dispatched to invest him as king.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，其貢使蔡璟言：「祖父本福建南安人，為琉球通事，傳至璟，擢長史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua, their tribute envoy Cai Jing said: "My grandfather was originally a man of Nan'an in Fujian, serving as a Ryukyu interpreter; the office passed down to Jing, who was promoted to chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 5 their tribute envoy Cai Jing petitioned: "My grandfather was a native of Nan'an in Fujian who served as a Ryukyu interpreter; the post passed to me, and I was promoted to chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 乞如制賜誥贈封其父母。」

translations.literal: I beg that, in accordance with regulations, patents of ennoblement be bestowed posthumously to ennoble my parents."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that his parents be posthumously ennobled with patents of office, as the regulations provided.

sentences.zh: 章下禮官，以無例而止。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the rites officials, who stopped the matter for lack of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Board of Rites, which rejected it for want of precedent.

sentences.zh: 明年，福建按察司言：「貢使程鵬至福州，與指揮劉玉私通貨賄，並宜究治。」

translations.literal: The next year, the Fujian surveillance commission said: "The tribute envoy Cheng Peng reached Fuzhou and privately traded bribes with the commander Liu Yu; both ought to be investigated and punished."
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Fujian surveillance commission reported that the tribute envoy Cheng Peng had reached Fuzhou and traded bribes in secret with the commander Liu Yu, and that both men should be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 命治玉而宥鵬。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was ordered punished while Peng was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was punished; Cheng Peng was spared.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，世子尚圓來告父喪，命給事中丘弘、行人韓文封為王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, the heir Shang Yuan came to announce his father's death; the supervising secretary Qiu Hong and the credential bearer Han Wen were ordered to invest him as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chenghua 7 the heir Shang Yuan reported his father's death, and Qiu Hong and Han Wen were sent to invest him as king.

sentences.zh: 弘至山東病卒，命給事中官榮代之。

translations.literal: Hong reached Shandong and died of illness; the supervising secretary Guan Rong was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Hong fell ill and died in Shandong; Guan Rong was appointed supervising secretary in his place.

sentences.zh: 十年，貢使至福建，殺懷安民夫婦二人，焚屋劫財，捕之不獲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, tribute envoys reached Fujian, killed two villagers of Huai'an, husband and wife, burned their house and plundered their property; captured they were not.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year tribute envoys reached Fujian, murdered a Huai'an couple, burned their house, and looted their goods; they were never caught.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢，禮官因請定令二年一貢，毋過百人，不得附攜私物，騷擾道途。

translations.literal: The next year they presented tribute again; the rites officials therefore requested that a regulation be fixed: tribute once every two years, no more than one hundred persons, no carrying private goods attached, no harassing the routes.
translations.idiomatic: When they came again with tribute the next year, the rites officials asked that a fixed rule be set: tribute every two years, no more than one hundred men, no private goods carried along, and no harassment of the roads.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，賜敕戒王。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and bestowed an imperial letter admonishing the king.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent an imperial letter of admonition to the king.

sentences.zh: 其使者請如祖制，比年一貢，不許。

translations.literal: Their envoys requested that, in accordance with the ancestral institution, tribute be annual; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys asked to revert to the ancestral practice of annual tribute; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 又明年，貢使至，會冊立東宮，請如朝鮮、安南，賜詔齎回。

translations.literal: The year after that, tribute envoys arrived; it happened that the eastern palace was being invested, and they requested that, like Korea and Annam, an edict be bestowed to carry back.
translations.idiomatic: The next year tribute envoys arrived just as a crown prince was being invested; they asked, as Korea and Annam had received, for an edict to carry home.

sentences.zh: 禮官議：琉球與日本、佔城並居海外，例不頒詔，乃降敕以文錦、彩幣賜其王及妃。

translations.literal: The rites officials deliberated: Ryukyu, together with Japan and Champa, all lay beyond the sea; by precedent edicts were not promulgated to them; they therefore issued an imperial letter and bestowed patterned brocade and colored silks on their king and consort.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials ruled that Ryukyu, like Japan and Champa, lay overseas and by precedent did not receive promulgated edicts; instead an imperial letter was issued, and patterned brocade and colored silks were granted to the king and queen.

sentences.zh: 十三年，使臣來，復請比年一貢，不許。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year envoys came and again requested annual tribute; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year envoys came and again asked for annual tribute; again they were refused.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，王卒，世子尚真來告喪，乞嗣爵，復請比年一貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year the king died; the heir Shang Zhen came to announce the death, begged to succeed to the title, and again requested annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year the king died; the heir Shang Zhen reported the death, sought succession to the title, and once more requested annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮官言，其國連章奏請，不過欲圖市易。

translations.literal: The rites officials said their state had sent memorial after memorial, seeking nothing more than to gain opportunities for trade.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials observed that the state's repeated petitions sought nothing beyond easier access to trade.

sentences.zh: 近年所遣之使，多系閩中逋逃罪人，殺人縱火，奸狡百端，專貿中國之貨，以擅外蕃之利，所請不可許。

translations.literal: Envoys dispatched in recent years were mostly fugitive criminals from Fujian who had fled their punishments—murdering, setting fires, full of crafty deceit, specializing in trading China's goods to monopolize profits in foreign lands; what they requested could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years most of the envoys sent had been fugitive criminals from Fujian—murderers and arsonists, endlessly cunning—who trafficked in Chinese goods to seize profits abroad; their request could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 乃命給事中董旻、行人張祥往封，而不從其請。

translations.literal: Dong Min and Zhang Xiang were then ordered to go and perform the investiture, but their request was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Min and Zhang Xiang were dispatched to perform the investiture, but the annual-tribute request was rejected.

sentences.zh: 十六年，使來，復引《祖訓》條章請比年一貢，帝賜敕戒約之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year envoys came and again cited provisions of the 《Ancestral Admonitions》 to request annual tribute; the emperor bestowed an imperial letter admonishing and restraining them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year envoys came again, citing the 《Ancestral Admonitions》 to ask for annual tribute; the emperor sent an admonitory letter restraining them.

sentences.zh: 十八年，使者至，復以為言，賜敕如初。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year envoys arrived and again raised the matter; an imperial letter was bestowed as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year envoys raised the same issue again and received the same admonitory letter as before.

sentences.zh: 使者攜陪臣子五人來受學，命隸南京國子監。

translations.literal: The envoys brought five sons of attending ministers to receive instruction; they were ordered enrolled in the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys brought five sons of attending ministers to study and were enrolled in the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，貢使來，其王移咨禮部，請遣五人歸省，從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year tribute envoys came; their king sent a note to the Ministry of Rites requesting that the five be sent home for family visits; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year tribute envoys arrived; the king wrote to the Ministry of Rites asking that the five students be allowed home on leave, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年從禮官議，敕琉球二年一貢如舊制，不得過百五十人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, following the rites officials' deliberation, an imperial letter ordered Ryukyu to tribute once every two years as under the old institution, with no more than one hundred fifty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2, following the rites officials' recommendation, an imperial letter restored Ryukyu's biennial tribute under the old rule, capped at one hundred fifty persons.

sentences.zh: 五年，尚真卒，其世子尚清以六年來貢，因報訃，使者還至海，溺死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shang Zhen died; his heir Shang Qing came with tribute in the sixth year and also reported the bereavement; the envoys, on returning, reached the sea and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Shang Zhen died; his heir Shang Qing came with tribute in the sixth year bearing news of the death, but the envoys drowned at sea on the return voyage.

sentences.zh: 九年遣他使來貢，並請封。

translations.literal: In the ninth year other envoys were dispatched to present tribute and also requested investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year other envoys were sent with tribute and also requested investiture.

sentences.zh: 命福建守臣勘報。

translations.literal: Fujian frontier officials were ordered to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian frontier officials were ordered to investigate and report back.

sentences.zh: 十一年，世子以國中臣民狀來上，乃命給事中陳侃、行人高澄持節往封。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the heir submitted a petition from ministers and people of the state; Chen Kan and Gao Cheng were then ordered to proceed with credentials to perform the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the heir submitted a petition from the state's officials and people; Chen Kan and Gao Cheng were then sent with credentials to perform the investiture.

sentences.zh: 及還，卻其贈。

translations.literal: On their return, their gifts were refused.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the gifts they had been offered were declined.

sentences.zh: 十四年，貢使至，仍以所贈黃金四十兩進於朝，乃敕侃等受之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year tribute envoys arrived and still presented to the court the forty taels of gold they had been given; the emperor then ordered Kan and the others to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year tribute envoys arrived and still brought the forty taels of gold they had been given, presenting it at court; the emperor then ordered Chen Kan and his party to accept it.

sentences.zh: 二十九年來貢，攜陪臣子五人入國學。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year they came with tribute, bringing five sons of attending ministers to enter the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year they came with tribute, bringing five sons of attending ministers to enter the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，貢使來，告王尚清之喪。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year tribute envoys came and announced the death of King Shang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year tribute envoys arrived bearing news of King Shang Qing's death.

sentences.zh: 先是，倭寇自浙江敗還，抵琉球境。

translations.literal: Earlier, Japanese pirates, defeated and returning from Zhejiang, reached Ryukyu territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Japanese pirates beaten back from Zhejiang had fled to Ryukyu waters.

sentences.zh: 世子尚元遣兵邀擊，大殲之，獲中國被掠者六人，至是送還。

translations.literal: The heir Shang Yuan sent troops to intercept and attack them, slaughtering them in great numbers; six Chinese who had been carried off were captured and, at this time, were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Shang Yuan sent troops to intercept them, inflicting heavy losses, and recovered six Chinese captives who were now sent home.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠順，賜賚有加，即命給事中郭汝霖、行人李際春封尚元為王。

translations.literal: The emperor praised their loyalty and submission, giving rewards and gifts beyond the usual; he immediately ordered Guo Rulin and Li Jichun to invest Shang Yuan as king.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised their loyalty, added extra gifts, and at once dispatched Guo Rulin and Li Jichun to invest Shang Yuan as king.

sentences.zh: 至福建，阻風未行。

translations.literal: Reaching Fujian, they were held up by contrary winds and did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Fujian but were stalled by contrary winds and could not sail on.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，其貢使亦至福建，稱受世子命，以海中風濤叵測，倭寇又出沒無時，恐天使有他慮，請如正德中封佔城故事，遣人代進表文方物，而身偕本國長史齎回封冊，不煩天使遠臨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year their tribute envoys also reached Fujian, stating they had received the heir's orders: because winds and waves at sea were unpredictable and Japanese pirates appeared and vanished at no fixed time, fearing the imperial envoy might have other concerns, they requested that, following the precedent of investing Champa in the Zhengde reign, someone be sent to submit the memorial and local products on their behalf, while they themselves together with their state's chief secretary would carry back the investiture patent and register, sparing the imperial envoy a distant journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year their tribute envoys also reached Fujian with orders from the heir: seas were unpredictable, Japanese pirates roved without warning, and they feared the imperial envoy might come to harm; they asked, following the Zhengde precedent for investing Champa, that someone else submit the memorial and tribute on their behalf while they themselves, with their chief secretary, carried home the patent of investiture—sparing the envoy the long voyage.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史樊獻科以聞，禮官言：「遣使冊封，祖制也。

translations.literal: The touring censor Fan Xianke reported this; the rites officials said: "Sending envoys to perform investiture is the ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Fan Xianke reported the request; the rites officials replied: "Dispatching envoys to invest a king is the ancestral institution.

sentences.zh: 今使者欲遙受冊命，是委君貺於草莽，不可一。

translations.literal: Now the envoys wish to receive investiture mandate from afar—this is to leave the sovereign's gifts in the wilds; this is impermissible, one.
translations.idiomatic: For the envoys now to seek investiture from afar would be to cast the sovereign's gift into the wilderness. That may not be allowed—first.

sentences.zh: 使者本奉表朝貢，乃求遣官代進，是棄世子專遣之命，不 可二。

translations.literal: The envoys originally came to present memorials and tribute, yet now ask that officials be sent to submit on their behalf—this is to discard the heir's specific order of dispatch; this is impermissible, two.
translations.idiomatic: They came to court to present memorials and tribute, yet now ask officials to submit in their place—contravening the heir's express commission. That may not be allowed—second.

sentences.zh: 昔正德中，佔城王為安南所侵，竄居他所，故使者齎回敕命，出一時權宜。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Zhengde reign, the king of Champa was invaded by Annam and fled to dwell elsewhere; therefore envoys carried back the investiture mandate—a measure of temporary expediency.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, the king of Champa was driven out by Annam and lived in exile; only then did envoys carry home the investiture mandate—a temporary expedient.

sentences.zh: 今援失國之事，以儗其君，不可三。

translations.literal: Now citing the matter of a lost state to compare with their king—this is impermissible, three.
translations.idiomatic: To invoke a king who had lost his realm as a precedent for their sovereign is inadmissible—third.

sentences.zh: 梯航通道，柔服之常。

translations.literal: Ladder-and-ship routes open channels; gentle submission is the constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Opening routes by ladder and ship, and coming in gentle submission—that is the constant practice.

sentences.zh: 彼所藉口者倭寇之警、風濤之險爾，不知琛賨之輸納、使臣之往來，果何由而得無患乎？

translations.literal: What they take as their excuse is merely warnings of Japanese pirates and the peril of winds and waves—do they not know how tribute treasures are delivered and envoys come and go, and by what means these could truly be free of trouble?
translations.idiomatic: They plead only pirate alarms and stormy seas—yet do tribute goods reach court and envoys travel back and forth entirely without hazard?

sentences.zh: 不可四。

translations.literal: This is impermissible, four.
translations.idiomatic: That may not be allowed—fourth.

sentences.zh: 曩佔城雖領封，其王猶懇請遣使。

translations.literal: Formerly Champa, though it received investiture, its king still earnestly requested that envoys be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Champa received investiture by courier, its king still earnestly asked that envoys be sent.

sentences.zh: 今使者非世子面命，又無印信文移。

translations.literal: Now these envoys have no face-to-face command from the heir, and no seal or written dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: These envoys bear no face-to-face command from the heir and no sealed dispatch.

sentences.zh: 若輕信其言，倘世子以遣使為至榮，遙拜為非禮，不肯受封，復上書請使，將誰執其咎？

translations.literal: If their words are lightly believed, should the heir hold that sending envoys is the highest honor and receiving investiture from afar is improper ritual, refuse the investiture, and again memorialize requesting envoys—who would bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: If we trust them lightly and the heir then holds that an envoy's arrival is the highest honor while distant investiture is unseemly, refuses the patent, and petitions again for an envoy—who will answer for it?

sentences.zh: 不可五。

translations.literal: This is impermissible, five.
translations.idiomatic: That may not be allowed—fifth.

sentences.zh: 乞命福建守臣仍以前詔從事。

translations.literal: We beg that Fujian frontier officials be ordered still to proceed according to the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Fujian frontier officials be ordered to proceed under the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 至未受封而先謝恩，亦非故事。

translations.literal: As for offering thanks for grace before receiving investiture—that too is not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: To offer thanks for grace before investiture has been received is also without precedent.

sentences.zh: 宜止聽其入貢，其謝恩表文，俟世子受封后遣使上進，庶中國之大體以全。」

translations.literal: They should simply be allowed to enter with tribute; their thanks-for-grace memorial should wait until after the heir receives investiture, when envoys may be sent to submit it—then the great propriety of China may be preserved whole."
translations.idiomatic: They should be allowed only to present tribute; the thanks-for-grace memorial should wait until after the heir has received investiture and can send envoys to submit it—so that China's larger propriety remains intact.

sentences.zh: 帝如其言。

translations.literal: The emperor followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四十一年夏，遣使入貢謝恩。

translations.literal: In the summer of the forty-first year envoys were sent to present tribute and thank for grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the forty-first year envoys came with tribute to express thanks.

sentences.zh: 明年及四十四年併入貢。

translations.literal: The next year and the forty-fourth year they presented tribute together.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again the next year and once more in the forty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，凡三貢，皆送還中國飄流人口。

translations.literal: During Longqing, they presented tribute three times in all, each time returning drift castaways from China.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign they sent tribute three times, each mission returning Chinese castaways adrift at sea.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉其忠誠，賜敕獎勵，加賚銀幣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised their loyalty and sincerity, bestowed an imperial letter of encouragement, and added gifts of silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised their loyalty, sent a letter of encouragement, and added gifts of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年冬，其國世子尚永遣使告父喪，請襲爵。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Wanli, the heir Shang Yong of their state sent envoys to announce his father's death and request succession to the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 1 the heir Shang Yong sent envoys to report his father's death and seek succession.

sentences.zh: 章下禮部，行福建守臣核奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites, which instructed Fujian frontier officials to verify and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of Rites, which directed Fujian officials to verify the facts and report.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使賀登極。

translations.literal: The next year envoys were sent to congratulate the accession.
translations.idiomatic: The following year envoys were sent to congratulate the new emperor on his accession.

sentences.zh: 三年入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year they entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年春，再貢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year they presented tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 七月命戶科給事中蕭崇業、行人謝傑齎敕及皮弁冠服、玉珪，封尚永為中山王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Xiao Chongye of the revenue section and Xie Jie the credential bearer were ordered to carry an imperial letter together with the leather cap and court robes and jade tablet, and invest Shang Yong as king of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xiao Chongye, supervising secretary of the revenue section, and Xie Jie the credential bearer were sent with an imperial letter, leather cap and court robes, and jade tablet to invest Shang Yong as king of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，崇業等未至，世子復遣使入貢，其後，修貢如常儀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the next year, before Chongye and the others had arrived, the heir again sent envoys to present tribute; thereafter tribute was maintained according to the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter, before Chongye's party had arrived, the heir sent tribute again; thereafter the tribute schedule resumed as usual.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，遣陪臣子三人入南京國學。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year three sons of attending ministers were sent to enter the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth winter three sons of attending ministers were sent to study at the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十九年遣使來貢，而尚永隨卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year envoys were sent to present tribute, and Shang Yong died soon after.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year envoys came with tribute; Shang Yong died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 禮官以日本方侵噬鄰境，琉球不可無王，乞令世子速請襲封，用資鎮壓。

translations.literal: The rites officials, because Japan was then invading and devouring neighboring territories and Ryukyu could not be without a king, begged that the heir be ordered quickly to request succession investiture, to serve in restraining and suppressing.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials, noting that Japan was encroaching on neighboring lands and that Ryukyu could not be left without a king, asked that the heir be urged to seek investiture quickly as a stabilizing measure.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，世子尚寧遣人請襲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the heir Shang Ning sent persons to request succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the heir Shang Ning sent envoys to request succession.

sentences.zh: 福建巡撫許孚遠以倭氛未息，據先臣鄭曉領封之議，請遣官一員齎敕至福建，聽其陪臣面領歸國，或遣習海武臣一人，偕陪臣同往。

translations.literal: The Fujian grand coordinator Xu Fuyuan, because the Japanese menace had not subsided, citing the deliberation of the former minister Zheng Xiao on receiving investiture in person, requested that one official be sent to carry an imperial letter to Fujian and allow their attending ministers to receive it face to face and return home, or that one military official experienced at sea be sent to go together with attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Xu Fuyuan, citing former minister Zheng Xiao's proposal because Japanese raids had not ceased, asked that one official carry the investiture letter to Fujian for the attending ministers to receive in person and return home—or else that one sea-seasoned military officer go with them.

sentences.zh: 禮官范謙議如其言，且請待世子表至乃許。

translations.literal: The rites official Fan Qian deliberated as he said, and further requested that they wait until the heir's memorial arrived before granting permission.
translations.idiomatic: Rites official Fan Qian endorsed the proposal and added that permission should wait until the heir's memorial arrived.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，世子以表至，其陪臣請如祖制遣官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the heir's memorial arrived; their attending ministers requested that envoys be sent as under the ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the heir's memorial arrived; his attending ministers asked that envoys be sent as ancestral practice required.

sentences.zh: 禮官余繼登言：「累朝冊封琉球，伐木造舟，動經數歲。

translations.literal: The rites official Yu Jideng said: "Investitures of Ryukyu across successive reigns—felling timber and building ships—often took several years.
translations.idiomatic: Rites official Yu Jideng argued: "Across successive reigns, Ryukyu investitures required felling timber and building ships and often took years.

sentences.zh: 使者蹈風濤之險，小國苦供億之煩。

translations.literal: Envoys braved the peril of winds and waves; the small state suffered the burden of provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys risked storms at sea; the small kingdom bore the cost of provisioning them.

sentences.zh: 宜一如前議從事。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to proceed entirely as in the previous deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: We should proceed entirely as in the earlier proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝可之，命今後冊封，止遣廉勇武臣一人偕請封陪臣前往，其祭前王，封新王，禮儀一如舊章，仍命俟彼國大臣結狀至乃行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this and ordered that henceforth for investiture only one upright and brave military official should be sent together with the attending ministers requesting investiture; rites for sacrificing to the previous king and investing the new king would follow the old regulations entirely; still they were ordered to wait until a bond from that state's ministers arrived before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ruled that henceforth investiture missions would send only one upright, brave military officer together with the attending ministers who had requested it; rites honoring the late king and investing the new one would follow the old code, but the mission would wait until a sworn affidavit from the kingdom's ministers arrived.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，貢使以狀至，仍請遣文臣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the next year tribute envoys arrived with the bond and still requested that civil officials be sent.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn tribute envoys arrived with the affidavit and still asked for civil officials to be dispatched.

sentences.zh: 乃命給事中洪瞻祖、行人王士禎往，且 命待海寇息警，乃渡海行事。

translations.literal: Hong Zhanzu and Wang Shizhen were then ordered to go, and they were further ordered to wait until sea pirates had quieted before crossing the sea to conduct the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhanzu and Wang Shizhen were then ordered to go, with instructions to wait until piracy on the seas had subsided before crossing to complete the investiture.

sentences.zh: 已而瞻祖以憂去，改命給事中夏子陽，以三十一年二月抵福建。

translations.literal: Before long Zhanzu left office due to bereavement; Xia Ziyang was appointed supervising secretary in his place, and in the second month of the thirty-first year arrived at Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzu soon left office to mourn a parent; Xia Ziyang replaced him as supervising secretary and reached Fujian in the second month of the thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 按臣方元彥復以海上多事，警報頻仍，會巡撫徐學聚疏請仍遣武臣。

translations.literal: The surveillance official Fang Yuanyan again reported that affairs at sea were numerous and alarms frequent; together with Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju he memorialized requesting that a military official still be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Fang Yuanyan again reported turmoil at sea and repeated alarms; he and grand coordinator Xu Xueju jointly memorialized asking that a military officer be sent instead.

sentences.zh: 子陽、士禎則以屬國言不可爽，使臣義當有終，乞堅成命慰遠人。

translations.literal: Ziyang and Shizhen, however, argued that a dependent state's word could not be broken and an envoy's duty must be carried through to the end, begging that the established command be firmly upheld to comfort those afar.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Ziyang and Wang Shizhen countered that a tributary state's trust must not be broken and an envoy's commission must be seen through, and begged that the original order stand to reassure those afar.

sentences.zh: 章俱未報，禮部侍郎李廷機言：「宜行領封初旨，並武臣不必遣。」

translations.literal: Neither memorial had yet received reply when Vice Minister of Rites Li Tingji said: "The initial order on receiving investiture in person should be followed, and a military official need not be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Before either memorial received a reply, Vice Minister of Rites Li Tingji argued: "The original plan for receiving investiture in person should stand, and no military officer need be sent.

sentences.zh: 於是御史錢桓、給事中蕭近高交章爭其不可，謂：「此事當在欽命未定之前，不當在冊使既遣之後，宜敕所司速成海艘，勿誤今歲渡海之期。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Qian Huan and Supervising Secretary Xiao Jingao submitted memorials in succession protesting that this could not be done, saying: "This matter ought to have been decided before the imperial command was unsettled, not after the investiture envoys had already been dispatched; the responsible offices should be ordered quickly to complete sea vessels, lest this year's deadline for crossing the sea be missed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Huan and supervising secretary Xiao Jingao then submitted competing memorials, insisting this was wrong: "The question should have been settled before the imperial command was issued, not after envoys were already dispatched; the responsible offices must be ordered to finish the sea vessels at once so this year's crossing is not missed.

sentences.zh: 俟竣事覆命，然後定為畫一之規，先之以文告，令其領封海上，永為遵守。」

translations.literal: After the affair is completed and they report back, then a uniform rule may be fixed—first issuing a written proclamation ordering them to receive investiture at sea, to be forever observed."
translations.idiomatic: After the mission is completed and they report back, a single uniform rule can be set—first by proclamation ordering investiture received at sea, to be followed forever after.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 三十三年七月，乃命子陽等速渡海竣事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-third year, Ziyang and the others were then ordered quickly to cross the sea and complete the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirty-third year Xia Ziyang and his party were ordered to cross the sea at once and finish the investiture.

sentences.zh: 當是時，日本方強，有吞滅之意。

translations.literal: At that time Japan was growing strong and had designs of swallowing them up.
translations.idiomatic: Japan was then growing powerful and clearly intended to swallow the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 琉球外御強鄰，內修貢不絕。

translations.literal: Ryukyu defended against strong neighbors abroad and maintained unbroken tribute within.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu held off powerful neighbors abroad while keeping tribute flowing without interruption.

sentences.zh: 四十年，日本果以勁兵三千入其國，擄其王，遷其宗器，大掠而去。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year Japan indeed entered their state with three thousand crack troops, carried off their king, removed their ancestral vessels, and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year Japan invaded with three thousand crack troops, seized the king, carried off the royal regalia, and withdrew after extensive looting.

sentences.zh: 浙江總兵官楊宗業以聞，乞嚴飭海上兵備，從之。

translations.literal: Yang Zongye, regional commander of Zhejiang, reported this and begged that coastal defenses be strictly ordered; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang regional commander Yang Zongye reported the raid and asked that coastal defenses be tightened; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而其王釋歸，復遣使修貢，然其國殘破已甚，禮官乃定十年一貢之例。

translations.literal: Before long their king was released and returned; envoys were again sent to renew tribute—but their state was already grievously shattered, and the rites officials therefore fixed the precedent of tribute once every ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The king was soon released and tribute resumed, but the kingdom lay in ruins; the rites officials therefore set tribute at once every ten years.

sentences.zh: 明年修貢如故。

translations.literal: The next year they renewed tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent tribute again as before.

sentences.zh: 又明年再貢，福建守臣遵朝命卻還之，其使者怏怏而去。

translations.literal: The year after that they presented tribute again; Fujian frontier officials, obeying the court order, sent them back; the envoys departed resentfully.
translations.idiomatic: They came again the year after that, but Fujian officials, obeying court orders, turned them away; the envoys left in sullen resentment.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，日本有取雞籠山之謀，其地名台灣，密邇福建，尚寧遣使以聞，詔海上警備。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Japan had designs on Chicken Cage Mountain—its place name is Taiwan, close to Fujian; Shang Ning sent envoys to report this, and an edict ordered coastal alert and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year Japan plotted against Chicken Cage Mountain—known as Taiwan, close to Fujian; Shang Ning sent word, and the court ordered heightened coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年，尚寧已卒，其世子尚豐遣使請貢請封。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi, Shang Ning had already died; his heir Shang Feng sent envoys to request tribute and investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3 Shang Ning had died; his heir Shang Feng sent envoys requesting both tribute and investiture.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「舊制，琉球二年一貢，後為倭寇所破，改期十年。

translations.literal: The rites officials said: "Under the old institution Ryukyu presented tribute once every two years; later, shattered by Japanese pirates, the interval was changed to ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The rites officials noted: "Under the old rule Ryukyu tribute came every two years; after devastation by Japanese pirates the interval was lengthened to ten years.

sentences.zh: 今其國休養未久，暫擬五年一貢，俟新王冊封更議。」

translations.literal: Now their state has not long rested and recovered; tribute is temporarily set at once every five years, to be reconsidered after the new king is invested.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom has scarcely recovered; tribute is temporarily fixed at once every five years, to be reconsidered after the new king is invested.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 五年遣使入貢請封。

translations.literal: In the fifth year envoys were sent to present tribute and request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year envoys came with tribute and a request for investiture.

sentences.zh: 六年再貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they presented tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 是時中國多事，而科臣應使者亦憚行，故封典久稽。

translations.literal: At this time China had many troubles, and the censorial officials who received envoys also feared to travel, so the investiture rites were long delayed.
translations.idiomatic: China was beset by troubles, and the censorial officials assigned to meet envoys were reluctant to make the journey, so the investiture ceremony dragged on for years.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，貢使又至請封，命遣官如故事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, tribute envoys again arrived requesting investiture; the court ordered officials dispatched according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 tribute envoys came again to request investiture, and the court ordered envoys sent as before.

sentences.zh: 禮官何如寵復以履險糜費，請令陪臣領封。

translations.literal: The rites official He Ruchong again cited the dangers and wasted expense of the journey and requested that attendant ministers receive the investiture in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: The rites official He Ruchong again argued that the mission was perilous and wasteful and asked that Ryukyuan ministers be allowed to receive investiture on the king's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，乃命戶科給事中杜三策、行人楊掄往，成禮而還。

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree and instead ordered Du San'e, supervising secretary of the Household Section, and the credential bearer Yang Lun to go; they completed the rites and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and sent Du San'e of the Household Section and the envoy Yang Lun to perform the ceremony; they completed the rites and returned.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，遣使賀東宮冊立。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, envoys were sent to congratulate the investiture of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year envoys were sent to congratulate the crown prince on his investiture.

sentences.zh: 自是，迄崇禎末，並修貢如儀。

translations.literal: From then until the end of Chongzhen, they continued to maintain tribute according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the fall of the dynasty they continued to send tribute on schedule.

sentences.zh: 後兩京繼沒，唐王立於福建，猶遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: Later, when both capitals fell in succession and the Prince of Tang was established in Fujian, envoys were still sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Even after both capitals fell and the Prince of Tang set up court in Fujian, Ryukyu still sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 其虔事天朝，為外籓最雲。

translations.literal: Their reverent service to the Celestial Court made them the most renowned of the outer vassal states.
translations.idiomatic: In their devotion to the dynasty they surpassed every other tributary state.

sentences.zh: 呂宋居南海中，去漳州甚近。

translations.literal: Luzon lay in the southern sea, very close to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luzon lay in the South China Sea, not far from Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年正月遣使偕瑣裡諸國來貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Hongwu, envoys were sent together with Suoli and other states to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Hongwu 5 it sent envoys with Suoli and other states to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年十月遣官齎詔，撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yongle, officials were sent bearing an edict to comfort and instruct the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 3 the court sent officials with an edict to reassure and instruct the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 八年與馮嘉施蘭入貢，自後久不至。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it came with Pangasinan to present tribute; after that it long did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year it presented tribute together with Pangasinan, then ceased coming for many years.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年，官軍追海寇林道乾至其國，國人助討有功，復朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli, when government troops pursued the sea bandit Lin Daoqian to that state, the people helped suppress him with merit and tribute to court resumed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 4, when Ming troops pursued the pirate Lin Daoqian to Luzon, the locals helped defeat him; tribute was restored.

sentences.zh: 時佛郎機強，與呂宋互市，久之見其國弱可取，乃奉厚賄遺王，乞地如牛皮大，建屋以居。

translations.literal: At the time the Folangji were strong and traded with Luzon; after long acquaintance they saw that the state was weak and could be taken, so they offered heavy bribes to the king and begged for land as large as a cowhide on which to build dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The Portuguese were then powerful and traded with Luzon; seeing the kingdom's weakness, they bribed the king and asked for a plot of land no larger than a cowhide on which to build a settlement.

sentences.zh: 王不虞其詐而許之，其人乃裂牛皮，聯屬至數千丈，圍呂宋地，乞如約。

translations.literal: The king did not expect their deceit and agreed; they cut the cowhide into strips and joined them to several thousand zhang, encircled Luzon territory, and demanded the land as promised.
translations.idiomatic: The king, unsuspecting, agreed; they cut the hide into strips, joined them into a cord thousands of feet long, and laid claim to a vast tract of Luzon.

sentences.zh: 王大駭，然業已許諾，無可奈何，遂聽之，而稍徵其稅如國法。

translations.literal: The king was greatly alarmed, but having already given his promise he could do nothing and so allowed it, while levying taxes on them slightly according to the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The king was horrified, but bound by his word he could only acquiesce, though he did levy taxes on them as the law allowed.

sentences.zh: 其人既得地，即營室築城，列火器，設守禦具，為窺伺計。

translations.literal: Once they had obtained the land, they immediately built houses and fortifications, arrayed firearms, and set out defensive equipment in preparation to spy and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had the land, they built houses and fortifications, deployed firearms, and prepared defenses for the conquest they were planning.

sentences.zh: 已，竟乘其無備，襲殺其王，逐其人民，而據其國，名仍呂宋，實佛郎機也。

translations.literal: Before long they took advantage of the state's unpreparedness, raided and killed the king, drove out the people, and seized the country; the name remained Luzon, but in fact it was Folangji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they struck without warning, killed the king, drove out the people, and seized the kingdom. It was still called Luzon, but it was Portuguese territory now.

sentences.zh: 先是，閩人以其地近且饒富，商販者至數萬人，往往久居不返，至長子孫。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the place was close and rich, Fujian merchants had numbered in the tens of thousands; many long stayed without returning, even raising children and grandchildren there.
translations.idiomatic: For years Fujian traders had settled there by the tens of thousands, lured by proximity and wealth; many never went home and raised families on the island.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機既奪其國，其王遣一酋來鎮，慮華人為變，多逐之歸，留者悉被其侵辱。

translations.literal: After the Folangji seized the state, their king sent a chieftain to garrison it; fearing that the Chinese might revolt, he drove most of them back, and those who remained were all subjected to insult and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: After the Portuguese takeover their governor expelled most of the Chinese settlers for fear of rebellion; those who remained were abused and humiliated.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月，酋郎雷敝裡系朥侵美洛居，役華人二百五十助戰。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year, the chieftain Lang Lei Bi Li Xi Lang invaded Maluku and conscripted two hundred fifty Chinese to help in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Wanli 21 the governor Lang Lei Bi Li Xi Lang invaded Maluku with two hundred fifty Chinese pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 有潘和五者為其哨官。

translations.literal: One Pan Hewu served as his sentry officer.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Pan Hewu served as their scout officer.

sentences.zh: 蠻人日酣臥，而令華人操舟，稍怠，輒鞭撻，有至死者。

translations.literal: The natives slept drunk every day while ordering the Chinese to row the boats; at the slightest slackness they were whipped and beaten, and some were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The natives drank themselves into stupors while the Chinese rowed; the slightest lapse brought a beating, and some men were flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 和五曰：「叛死，箠死，等死耳，否亦且戰死，曷若刺殺此酋以救死。
