translations.literal: Hewu said, "To rebel is death, to be beaten is death -- equal deaths. Even if we refuse, we will die in battle anyway. Why not stab this chieftain to save our lives?
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hewu said, "Rebellion means death, and so does the lash -- either way we die. If we refuse, we'll die fighting anyway. Better to kill this governor and live.

sentences.zh: 勝則揚帆歸，不勝而見縛，死未晚也。」

translations.literal: If we win, we hoist sail and return; if we lose and are bound, death will not come too soon."
translations.idiomatic: If we win, we sail home. If we lose and are captured, we die -- but not before we've tried.

sentences.zh: 眾然之，乃夜刺殺其酋，持酋首大呼。

translations.literal: The crowd agreed; that night they stabbed and killed the chieftain, seized his head, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The others agreed. That night they killed the governor, held up his severed head, and shouted the alarm.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻驚起，不知所為，悉被刃，或落水死。

translations.literal: The natives started up in alarm, not knowing what to do; all were cut down by blades, or fell into the water and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The natives woke in panic and were cut down where they stood; others drowned trying to escape.

sentences.zh: 和五等盡收其金寶、甲仗，駕舟以歸。

translations.literal: Hewu and the others gathered all the gold, treasures, armor, and weapons and sailed home in the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hewu and his men seized the gold, arms, and treasure and sailed for home.

sentences.zh: 失路之安南，為其國人所掠，惟郭惟太等三十二人附他舟獲返。

translations.literal: They lost their way to Annam and were plundered by the people of that country; only Guo Weitai and thirty-two others, attaching themselves to other boats, managed to return.
translations.idiomatic: They lost their way to Annam and were robbed by locals; only Guo Weitai and thirty-two others, catching rides on other vessels, made it back.

sentences.zh: 時酋子郎雷貓吝駐朔霧，聞之，率眾馳至，遣僧陳父冤，乞還其戰艦、金寶，戮仇人以償父命。

translations.literal: At the time the chieftain's son Lang Lei Mao Lin was stationed at Shuowu; hearing of it, he led his men galloping there, sent a monk to state his father's grievance, and begged for the return of the warships and gold and treasures and for the enemies to be executed to avenge his father's life.
translations.idiomatic: The governor's son Lang Lei Mao Lin was then at Shuowu; hearing the news, he rushed over, sent a monk to plead his father's case, and demanded the return of the ships and treasure and the execution of the killers.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許孚遠聞於朝，檄兩廣督撫以禮遣僧，置惟太於理，和五竟留安南不敢返。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xu Fuyuan reported it to the court, ordered the governors of the two Guang provinces to send the monk back with courtesy, put Weitai on trial, and Hewu in the end remained in Annam and dared not return.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xu Fuyuan reported the affair; the two Guang governors were ordered to send the monk home courteously and put Guo Weitai on trial. Pan Hewu stayed in Annam and never dared return.

sentences.zh: 初，酋之被戮也，其部下居呂宋者，盡逐華人於城外，毀其廬。

translations.literal: At first, when the chieftain was killed, his subordinates residing in Luzon drove all the Chinese outside the city walls and destroyed their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor was killed, his men in Luzon expelled every Chinese settler beyond the walls and razed their homes.

sentences.zh: 及貓吝歸，令城外築室以居。

translations.literal: When Mao Lin returned, he ordered houses built outside the city for them to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Lin returned, he had houses built outside the walls for them to live in.

sentences.zh: 會有傳日本來寇者，貓吝懼交通為患，復議驅逐。

translations.literal: There happened to be rumors that Japan was coming to raid; Mao Lin feared that contact with them would bring trouble and again discussed expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread that Japan was about to attack; fearing collusion, Mao Lin again debated expelling the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 而孚遠適遣人招還，蠻乃給行糧遣之。

translations.literal: But Fuyuan happened to send men to summon them back, and the natives then supplied travel rations and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xu Fuyuan sent envoys to recall them, and the natives provisioned them for the journey and let them go.

sentences.zh: 然華商嗜利，趨死不顧，久之復成聚。

translations.literal: Yet Chinese merchants were addicted to profit and rushed toward death without regard; after long time they again formed a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: But Chinese traders, greedy for profit and heedless of danger, gradually drifted back until another settlement took shape.

sentences.zh: 其時礦稅使者四出，奸宄蜂起言利，有閻應龍、張嶷者，言呂宋機易山素產金銀，采之，歲可得金十萬兩、銀三十萬兩，以三十年七月詣闕奏聞，帝即納之。

translations.literal: At that time mining-tax envoys were going out in all directions and scoundrels swarmed forward speaking of profit; Yan Yinglong and Zhang Yi said that Jiyi Mountain in Luzon had always produced gold and silver and that, if mined, one year could yield one hundred thousand taels of gold and three hundred thousand taels of silver; in the seventh month of the thirtieth year they went to court to report this, and the emperor immediately accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Mining-tax commissioners were fanning out everywhere, and profiteers abounded. Yan Yinglong and Zhang Yi claimed that Mount Jiyi in Luzon was rich in gold and silver and could yield a hundred thousand taels of gold and three hundred thousand of silver a year. In the seventh month of Wanli 30 they presented this at court, and the emperor approved it at once.

sentences.zh: 命下，舉朝駭異。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, the whole court was shocked and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When the order went out, the entire court was appalled.

sentences.zh: 都御史溫純疏言：「近中外諸臣爭言礦稅之害，天聽彌高。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun memorialized, saying, "Recently officials at court and abroad have all contended over the harm of mining taxes, and the emperor's attention to the matter has grown ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun memorialized: "Recently officials at court and abroad have protested the harm of mining levies, and Your Majesty has heard them ever more clearly.

sentences.zh: 今廣東李鳳至污辱婦女六十六人，私運財賄至三十巨舟、三百大扛，勢必見戮於積怒之眾。

translations.literal: Now in Guangdong Li Feng has defiled sixty-six women and privately transported bribes in thirty huge boats and three hundred large loads; he is bound to be killed by the accumulated wrath of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong alone Li Feng has violated sixty-six women and smuggled bribes aboard thirty large ships and three hundred heavy loads. An enraged populace will surely kill him.

sentences.zh: 何如及今撤之，猶不失威福操縱之柄。

translations.literal: How much better to withdraw them now -- one still need not lose the handle of authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw the policy now and you will still keep control of power and favor.

sentences.zh: 緬酋以寶井故，提兵十萬將犯內地，西南之蠻，岌岌可憂。

translations.literal: The Burmese chieftain, because of the treasure wells, is raising one hundred thousand troops and is about to invade the interior; the barbarians of the southwest are precarious and cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese, fighting over gem mines, are massing a hundred thousand men to invade the interior. The southwest is already on the brink.

sentences.zh: 而閩中奸徒又以機易山事見告。

translations.literal: And scoundrels in Fujian have again reported the matter of Jiyi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fujian scoundrels have come forward with tales of Mount Jiyi.

sentences.zh: 此其妄言，真如戲劇，不意皇上之聰明而誤聽之。

translations.literal: This wild talk is truly like a play; I did not expect that Your Majesty's intelligence would mistakenly heed it.
translations.idiomatic: It is pure fantasy, fit for the stage -- yet Your Majesty's wise ear has been taken in.

sentences.zh: 臣等驚魂搖曳，寢食不寧。

translations.literal: We, your ministers, are shaken in soul; we cannot eat or sleep in peace.
translations.idiomatic: We lie awake in dread and cannot eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 異時變興禍起，費國家之財不知幾百萬，倘或剪滅不早，其患又不止費財矣。

translations.literal: When in the future trouble arises and disaster begins, the state's treasure spent will be who knows how many millions; if it is not cut down early, the harm will be more than wasted treasure.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster strikes, the treasury will bleed millions. Wait too long to act, and the cost will be far worse than money.

sentences.zh: 臣聞海澄市舶高采已歲徵三萬金，決不遺餘力而讓利。

translations.literal: I have heard that Gao Cai of Haicheng maritime trade already levies thirty thousand in gold each year and will certainly not spare any effort to yield profit.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cai at Haicheng already exacts thirty thousand taels of gold a year from maritime trade. He will not yield a penny of profit.

sentences.zh: 即機易越在海外，亦決無遍地金銀，任人採取之理，安所得金十萬、銀三十萬，以實其言。

translations.literal: Even if Jiyi is beyond the sea, there is certainly no principle of gold and silver everywhere for anyone to mine at will; how can one obtain one hundred thousand in gold and three hundred thousand in silver to substantiate their words?
translations.idiomatic: Even overseas, gold and silver do not lie open for the taking. Where are the hundred thousand taels of gold and three hundred thousand of silver to prove this claim?

sentences.zh: 不過假借朝命，闌出禁物，勾引諸番，以逞不軌之謀，豈止煩擾公私，貽害海澄一邑而已哉。

translations.literal: It is nothing but borrowing the court's mandate, smuggling forbidden goods, and enticing the various barbarians to carry out unorthodox plots -- how is the harm limited to troubling public and private interests and injuring the single county of Haicheng?
translations.idiomatic: They mean only to use imperial authority to smuggle contraband and incite the barbarians in treason. The damage will not stop at Haicheng or the public purse.

sentences.zh: 昔年倭患，正緣奸民下海，私通大姓，設計勒價，致倭賊憤恨，稱兵犯順。

translations.literal: In past years the Japanese calamity arose precisely because scoundrels went to sea, communicated privately with great clans, and designed price extortion, causing the Japanese pirates to grow resentful and raise troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese raids of years past began when local ruffians went to sea, colluded with powerful families, and rigged prices until the pirates turned violent.

sentences.zh: 今以朝命行之，害當彌大。

translations.literal: Now to carry it out by court mandate, the harm should be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Do the same under imperial orders and the harm will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 及乎兵連禍結，諸奸且效汪直、曾一本輩故智，負海稱王，擁兵列寨，近可以規重利，遠不失為尉佗。

translations.literal: When troops are linked and disasters knotted, the scoundrels will imitate the old tricks of Wang Zhi, Zeng Yiben, and their kind: relying on the sea to call themselves kings, gathering troops and setting up stockades -- near at hand they can scheme for heavy profit, and in the distance they need not fall short of being a Zhao Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: When war follows, these men will copy the pirates Wang Zhi and Zeng Yiben -- declaring themselves kings at sea, raising armies, building forts. Near at hand lies great profit; far off, a kingdom of their own like Zhao Tuo.

sentences.zh: 於諸亡命之計得矣，如國家大患何！

translations.literal: For the plans of the various fugitives this may succeed, but what of the state's great calamity!
translations.idiomatic: That may serve the outlaws well enough -- but what of the empire?

sentences.zh: 乞急置於理，用消禍本。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be urgently put on trial to eliminate the root of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that these men be tried at once and the source of this evil cut off."

sentences.zh: 言官金忠士、曹於汴、硃吾弼等亦連章力爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials Jin Zhongshi, Cao Yubian, Zhu Wubi, and others also submitted linked memorials arguing forcefully; all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Jin Zhongshi, Cao Yubian, Zhu Wubi, and others filed memorial after memorial in protest. The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 事下福建守臣，持不欲行，而迫於朝命，乃遣海澄丞王時和、百戶幹一成偕嶷往勘。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Fujian frontier officials, who held back and did not wish to proceed but, compelled by the court order, sent Haicheng Assistant Magistrate Wang Shihe, Company Officer Gan Yicheng, and Yi together to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to Fujian's frontier officials, who were reluctant to act but bowed to the court order and sent Haicheng Assistant Magistrate Wang Shihe, Company Officer Gan Yicheng, and Zhang Yi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 呂宋人聞之大駭。

translations.literal: The people of Luzon, hearing of it, were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Luzon heard, they were terrified.

sentences.zh: 華人流寓者謂之曰：「天朝無他意，特是奸徒橫生事端。

translations.literal: Chinese sojourners told them, "The Celestial Court has no other intent; it is merely that scoundrels have recklessly created an incident.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese residents reassured them: "The court means no harm. Scoundrels at home invented this affair.

sentences.zh: 今遣使者按驗，俾奸徒自窮，便於還報耳。」

translations.literal: Now envoys are sent to investigate and verify, so that the scoundrels will be cornered themselves and it will be easy to report back."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys have come only to investigate and expose the liars. That is all.

sentences.zh: 其酋意稍解，命諸僧散花道旁，若敬朝使，而盛陳兵衛迓之。

translations.literal: The chieftain's mind was slightly eased; he ordered the monks to scatter flowers along the roadside as if revering court envoys, and grandly arrayed military guards to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The governor's suspicions eased somewhat. Monks strewed flowers along the road as if greeting imperial envoys, and he received the mission with a great show of armed escort.

sentences.zh: 時和等入，酋為置宴，問曰：「天朝欲遣人開山。

translations.literal: When Shihe and the others entered, the chieftain set a banquet and asked, "The Celestial Court wishes to send men to open the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet the governor asked Wang Shihe, "So the court wants to open the mountains.

sentences.zh: 山各有主，安得開？

translations.literal: Each mountain has its master -- how can they be opened?
translations.idiomatic: Every mountain here has an owner. Who gave you leave to mine them?

sentences.zh: 譬中華有山，可容我國開耶？」

translations.literal: Suppose China had mountains -- would they allow our state to open them?"
translations.idiomatic: Would China let us come dig up your hills?

sentences.zh: 且言：「樹生金豆，是何樹所生？」

translations.literal: And he said, "Trees bear golden beans -- what tree bears them?"
translations.idiomatic: You say trees grow golden beans. Which trees are those?

sentences.zh: 時和不能對，數視嶷，嶷曰：「此地皆金，何必問豆所自？」

translations.literal: Shihe could not answer and repeatedly looked at Yi; Yi said, "This place is all gold -- why ask where the beans come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihe had no reply and kept glancing at Zhang Yi, who said, "The whole place is gold. Why quibble over beans?

sentences.zh: 上下皆大笑，留嶷，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Those above and below all laughed greatly; they detained Yi and wanted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The hall erupted in laughter. They detained Zhang Yi and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 諸華人共解，乃獲釋歸。

translations.literal: All the Chinese together interceded, and he was then released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese community interceded, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 時和還任，即病悸死。

translations.literal: Shihe returned to his post and immediately fell ill with palpitations and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihe returned to his post, fell ill with heart palpitations, and died.

sentences.zh: 守臣以聞，請治嶷妄言罪。

translations.literal: The frontier officials reported it and requested that Yi be punished for wild talk.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier officials reported the affair and asked that Zhang Yi be punished for his fabrications.

sentences.zh: 事已止矣，而呂宋人終自疑，謂天朝將襲取其國，諸流寓者為內應，潛謀殺之。

translations.literal: The matter had already stopped, but the people of Luzon remained suspicious themselves, saying that the Celestial Court would seize their state, that the sojourners would serve as inside collaborators, and secretly plotted to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis seemed over, but the Luzonese remained convinced that the dynasty meant to seize their kingdom with Chinese residents as fifth columnists, and they began plotting a massacre.

sentences.zh: 明年，聲言發兵侵旁國，厚價市鐵器。

translations.literal: The next year they proclaimed that troops would be sent to invade a neighboring state and offered high prices to buy ironware.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they announced a campaign against a neighbor and paid top prices for iron goods.

sentences.zh: 華人貪利盡鬻之，於是家無寸鐵。

translations.literal: The Chinese, greedy for profit, sold everything; thus every household was left without an inch of iron.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for profit, the Chinese sold every scrap of metal until not a household had a weapon left.

sentences.zh: 酋乃下令錄華人姓名，分三百人為一院，入即殲之。

translations.literal: The chieftain then ordered the recording of Chinese names and divided them into compounds of three hundred persons each; upon entering, they were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The governor then registered every Chinese name, grouped them in compounds of three hundred, and slaughtered each group as they were admitted.

sentences.zh: 事稍露，華人群走菜園。

translations.literal: When the matter leaked slightly, the Chinese fled in crowds to the vegetable gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Word leaked, and the Chinese fled en masse to the market gardens.

sentences.zh: 酋發兵攻，眾無兵仗，死無算，奔大侖山。

translations.literal: The chieftain sent troops to attack; the crowd had no weapons or armor, deaths were beyond counting, and they fled to Mount Dalun.
translations.idiomatic: Troops pursued them. Unarmed, they fell by the thousands and retreated to Mount Dalun.

sentences.zh: 蠻人復來攻，眾殊死鬥，蠻兵少挫。

translations.literal: The natives came again to attack; the crowd fought to the death and the native troops were slightly repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: The natives attacked again; the Chinese fought desperately and briefly drove them back.

sentences.zh: 酋旋悔，遣使議和。

translations.literal: The chieftain soon regretted it and sent an envoy to discuss peace.
translations.idiomatic: The governor soon regretted the bloodshed and sent an envoy to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 眾疑其偽，撲殺之。

translations.literal: The crowd suspected deception and beat and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The refugees suspected a trick and killed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 酋大怒，斂眾入城，設伏城旁。

translations.literal: The chieftain was greatly angered, gathered his forces into the city, and set an ambush beside it.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the governor withdrew into the city and laid an ambush outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 眾飢甚，悉下山攻城。

translations.literal: The crowd was extremely hungry and all descended the mountain to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, they came down from the mountain and stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 伏發，眾大敗，先後死者二萬五千人。

translations.literal: The ambush was sprung; the crowd was greatly defeated, and those who died before and after numbered twenty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The trap was sprung. Twenty-five thousand Chinese were killed.

sentences.zh: 酋尋出令，諸所掠華人貲，悉封識貯庫。

translations.literal: The chieftain soon issued an order that all property plundered from the Chinese was to be sealed, marked, and stored in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The governor then ordered all seized Chinese property sealed and stored in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 移書閩中守臣，言華人將謀亂，不得已先之，請令死者家屬往取其孥與帑。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to the frontier officials of Fujian, saying that the Chinese were about to plot rebellion and that he had no choice but to strike first, and requesting that the families of the dead be allowed to come and take their wives, children, and funds.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Fujian's officials claiming the Chinese had been plotting rebellion and that he had acted first, and invited the victims' families to come collect their kin and goods.

sentences.zh: 巡撫徐學聚等亟告變於朝，帝驚悼，下法司議奸徒罪。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju urgently reported the disaster to the court; the emperor was shocked and grieved and ordered the judicial offices to deliberate on the scoundrels' crime.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju rushed word to court. The emperor was horrified and ordered the judiciary to determine the profiteers' punishment.

sentences.zh: 三十二年十二月議上，帝曰：「嶷等欺誑朝廷，生釁海外，致二萬商民盡膏鋒刃，損威辱國，死有餘辜，即梟首傳示海上。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirty-second year the deliberation was submitted; the emperor said, "Yi and the others deceived and misled the court, created conflict overseas, and caused twenty thousand merchants and people to grease the blades; they damaged prestige and humiliated the state and deserve death with guilt to spare -- let them be beheaded at once and their heads displayed at sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Wanli 32 the verdict reached the throne. The emperor declared, "Zhang Yi and his accomplices lied to the court, provoked bloodshed overseas, and sent twenty thousand merchants and civilians to their deaths, shaming the empire. Execute them and display their heads along the coast.

sentences.zh: 呂宋酋擅殺商民，撫按官議罪以聞。」

translations.literal: The chieftain of Luzon arbitrarily killed merchants; let the pacification officials deliberate on the crime and report."
translations.idiomatic: As for the Luzon governor who slaughtered merchants, let the frontier officials determine his punishment and report.

sentences.zh: 學聚等乃移檄呂宋，數以擅殺罪，令送死者妻子歸，竟不能討也。

translations.literal: Xueju and the others then sent a dispatch to Luzon, enumerating the crime of arbitrary killing and ordering that the wives and children of the dead be sent back; in the end they could not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueju dispatched a reprimand to Luzon demanding the return of the victims' families, but no punishment could be enforced.

sentences.zh: 其後，華人復稍稍往，而蠻人利中國互市，亦不拒，久之復成聚。

translations.literal: Afterward, Chinese again gradually went there, and because the natives profited from trade with China they did not refuse; after long time a settlement again formed.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese traders gradually returned, and the locals, eager for trade, did not turn them away. In time another settlement grew up.

sentences.zh: 時佛郎機已並滿剌加，益以呂宋，勢愈強，橫行海外，遂據廣東香山澳，築城以居，與民互市，而患復中於粵矣。

translations.literal: At the time the Folangji had already annexed Malacca and, with Luzon added, their power grew ever stronger; they ran rampant on the seas, then occupied Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong, built a city to dwell in, and traded with the people -- and disaster again struck Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Portuguese had taken Malacca and Luzon and grown ever bolder. They dominated the seas, seized Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong, built a fortified settlement, and traded with local merchants -- and trouble returned to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 合貓裡

translations.literal: Camarines Sur
translations.idiomatic: Camarines Sur

sentences.zh: 合貓裡，海中小國也。

translations.literal: Camarines Sur is a small state in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Camarines Sur was a small island kingdom.

sentences.zh: 土瘠多山，山外大海，饒魚蟲，人知耕稼。

translations.literal: The soil is barren and there are many mountains; beyond the mountains lies the great sea, rich in fish and insects; the people know how to farm.
translations.idiomatic: The land was poor and mountainous, but the surrounding seas teemed with fish; the people farmed.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年九月遣使附爪哇使臣朝貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Yongle, envoys were sent attached to the Java envoys to present tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongle 3 it sent envoys with the Javanese mission to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國又名貓裡務，近呂宋，商舶往來，漸成富壤。

translations.literal: The state was also called Maoliwu; it was near Luzon, and as merchant ships came and went it gradually became a rich land.
translations.idiomatic: It was also known as Maoliwu. Close to Luzon and on the shipping lanes, it grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 華人入其國，不敢欺陵，市法最平，故華人為之語曰：「若要富，須往貓裡務。」

translations.literal: When Chinese entered the state they did not dare bully or oppress; the market laws were the fairest, so the Chinese made a saying: "If you wish to grow rich, you must go to Maoliwu."
translations.idiomatic: Chinese traders were treated fairly and never cheated, and a saying went around: "Want to get rich? Go to Maoliwu.

sentences.zh: 有網巾礁老者，最凶悍，海上行劫，舟若飄風，遇之無免者。

translations.literal: There was an Old Man of Wangjin Reef, most fierce and brutal; he roved the sea robbing ships, and boats were like drifting wind -- none who met him escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A pirate called the Old Man of Wangjin Reef was the fiercest raider on the sea; ships that crossed his path were lost.

sentences.zh: 然特惡商舶不至其地，偶有至者，待之甚善。

translations.literal: Yet he especially hated merchant ships that did not come to his place; when any occasionally arrived, he treated them very well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he reserved his wrath for merchants who bypassed his waters; any who did call were treated with surprising hospitality.

sentences.zh: 貓裡務後遭寇掠，人多死傷，地亦貧困。

translations.literal: Later Maoliwu suffered bandit raids; many were killed or wounded, and the land also grew poor.
translations.idiomatic: Maoliwu was later ravaged by raiders. Many were killed or wounded, and the country fell into poverty.

sentences.zh: 商人慮為礁老所劫，鮮有赴者。

translations.literal: Merchants feared being robbed by the Old Man of the Reef and rarely went.
translations.idiomatic: Traders, fearing the Old Man of the Reef, seldom ventured there.

sentences.zh: 美洛居

translations.literal: Maluku
translations.idiomatic: Maluku

sentences.zh: 美洛居，俗訛為米六合，居東海中，頗稱饒富。

translations.literal: Maluku -- vulgarly corrupted to "Mi Liuhe" -- lies in the eastern sea and is quite called rich and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Maluku, vulgarly miscalled "Mi Liuhe," lay in the eastern sea and was regarded as notably prosperous.

sentences.zh: 酋出，威儀甚備，所部合掌伏道旁。

translations.literal: When the chieftain went out, his ceremonial display was very complete; those under his command pressed palms together and prostrated themselves beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the chieftain appeared in public, his retinue was arrayed in full ceremony, and his subjects pressed their palms together and prostrated themselves along the roadside.

sentences.zh: 男子削髮，，女椎結。

translations.literal: Men shaved their heads,, women wore chignons.
translations.idiomatic: Men shaved their heads,, and women wore their hair in topknots.

sentences.zh: 地有香山，雨後香墮，沿流滿地，居民拾取不竭。

translations.literal: The land had a Fragrant Mountain; after rain the fragrance fell, filling the streams and covering the ground along their course, and the inhabitants gathered it without end.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Fragrant Mountain on the island. After rain, aromatic droplets fell and washed down the streams until the ground along the banks was covered; the people gathered them endlessly.

sentences.zh: 其酋委積充棟，以待商舶之售。

translations.literal: The chieftain piled stores until they filled the rafters, waiting to sell them to merchant ships.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain stockpiled the spice until his storehouses overflowed, holding it for sale to passing merchant vessels.

sentences.zh: 東洋不產丁香，獨此地有之，可以闢邪，故華人多市易。

translations.literal: The Eastern Ocean did not produce cloves; this place alone had them, and they could ward off evil, so Chinese traded there in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Cloves were not produced elsewhere in the Eastern Ocean; only this island had them. Believed to dispel evil influences, they drew many Chinese traders.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，佛郎機來攻，其酋戰敗請降，乃宥令復位，歲以丁香充貢，不設戍兵而去。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, the Folangji came to attack; the chieftain was defeated in battle and begged to surrender, whereupon he was pardoned and restored to his throne; each year he paid tribute in cloves, and they departed without leaving garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign the Portuguese attacked. The chieftain was defeated and sued for peace; he was pardoned and restored to power on condition that cloves be sent as tribute each year, and the Portuguese withdrew without leaving a garrison.

sentences.zh: 已，紅毛番橫海上，知佛郎機兵已退，乘虛直抵城下，執其酋，語之曰：「若善事我，我為若主，殊勝佛郎機也。」

translations.literal: Before long the Red-Haired foreigners dominated the seas; learning that the Folangji troops had withdrawn, they seized the opportunity and went straight to the city walls, seized the chieftain, and said to him: "If you serve me well, I shall be your lord -- far better than the Folangji."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Dutch dominated the seas. Learning that the Portuguese had withdrawn, they seized the chance, sailed straight to the walls, took the chieftain captive, and told him, "Serve me faithfully and I will be your master -- a far better one than the Portuguese."

sentences.zh: 酋不得已聽命，復位如故。

translations.literal: The chieftain had no choice but to obey; he was restored to his throne as before.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain had no choice but to submit, and was reinstated as before.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機酋聞之大怒，率兵來攻，道為華人所殺，語具《呂宋傳》。

translations.literal: The Folangji chieftain, hearing this, was greatly enraged and led troops to attack; on the road he was killed by Chinese, the account being given in full in the 《Luzon Monograph》.
translations.idiomatic: The Portuguese governor, enraged at the news, marched to attack, but was killed en route by Chinese -- the full account appears in the 《Luzon Monograph》.

sentences.zh: 時紅毛番雖據美洛居，率一二歲率眾返國，既返復來。

translations.literal: At the time, although the Red-Haired foreigners held Maluku, every year or two they would lead their followers back to their country; once returned, they would come again.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Dutch held Maluku, every year or two they led their people home, only to return again afterward.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機酋子既襲位，欲竟父志，大舉兵來襲，值紅毛番已去，遂破美洛居，殺其酋，立己所親信主之。

translations.literal: After the Folangji chieftain's son had succeeded to the throne and wished to fulfill his father's ambition, he raised a great army and came to attack; finding the Red-Haired foreigners already gone, he then broke Maluku, killed its chieftain, and installed one of his trusted men to rule.
translations.idiomatic: The Portuguese governor's son, succeeding his father and intent on finishing what he had begun, launched a major assault. The Dutch had already left, so he overran Maluku, killed the chieftain, and installed a man of his own trust as ruler.

sentences.zh: 無何，紅毛番至，又破其城，逐佛郎機所立酋，而立美洛居故王之子。

translations.literal: Before long the Red-Haired foreigners arrived, broke the city again, drove out the chieftain installed by the Folangji, and installed the son of Maluku's former king.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Dutch returned, stormed the city again, expelled the Portuguese appointee, and restored the son of Maluku's former king.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲構兵，人不堪命。

translations.literal: From then on they raised arms every year, and the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two sides fought year after year, and the people could endure it no longer.

sentences.zh: 華人流寓者，遊說兩國，令各罷兵，分國中萬老高山為界，山以北屬紅毛番，南屬佛郎機，始稍休息，而美洛居竟為兩國所分。

translations.literal: Chinese sojourners there persuaded the two states to cease hostilities and divided the country at Mount Wanlao as boundary: north of the mountain belonged to the Red-Haired foreigners, south to the Folangji; only then did they rest somewhat, and Maluku was ultimately divided between the two states.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese residents brokered a truce and divided the island at Mount Wanlao: the north went to the Dutch, the south to the Portuguese. Only then did the fighting ease, and Maluku was permanently split between the two powers.

sentences.zh: 沙瑤，與吶嗶啴連壞。

translations.literal: Sayao and Napitan were contiguous territories.
translations.idiomatic: Sayao and Napitan were neighboring lands.

sentences.zh: 吶嗶啴在海畔，沙瑤稍紆入山隈，皆與呂宋近。

translations.literal: Napitan was on the seashore; Sayao wound slightly into a mountain recess; both were close to Luzon.
translations.idiomatic: Napitan lay on the coast, while Sayao stretched back into the hills; both were near Luzon.

sentences.zh: 男女蓄髮椎結，男子用履，婦女跣足。

translations.literal: Men and women kept their hair and wore topknots; men wore shoes, women went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Both sexes wore their hair long in topknots. Men wore shoes; women went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 以板為城，豎木覆茅為室。

translations.literal: They used planks for walls, erected timbers and thatched roofs for dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Their settlements were walled with planks; houses were framed with upright timbers and roofed with thatch.

sentences.zh: 崇釋教，多建禮拜寺。

translations.literal: They revered Buddhism and built many mosques.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Buddhism and built many houses of worship.

sentences.zh: 男女之禁甚嚴，夫行在前，其婦與人嘲笑，夫即刃其婦，所嘲笑之人不敢逃，任其刺割。

translations.literal: The prohibitions between men and women were very strict: if the husband walked ahead and his wife was mocked by someone, the husband would immediately blade his wife, and the one who had mocked her did not dare flee but let himself be stabbed and cut at will.
translations.idiomatic: Sexual propriety was strictly enforced. If a husband walked ahead and another man mocked his wife, the husband would immediately kill her; the mocker would not flee but submit to being stabbed and hacked at the husband's pleasure.

sentences.zh: 盜不問大小，輒論死。

translations.literal: Thieves, without distinction of magnitude, were invariably sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Theft, however petty, was always punished by death.

sentences.zh: 孕婦將產，以水灌之，且以水滌其子，置水中，生而與水習矣。

translations.literal: When a pregnant woman was about to give birth, she was doused with water, and her child was also washed with water and placed in water; from birth it was accustomed to water.
translations.idiomatic: When a woman was near delivery she was bathed in water; the newborn was washed and placed in water as well, so that from birth the child was at home in the water.

sentences.zh: 物產甚薄，華人商其地，所攜僅磁器、鍋釜之類，重者至布而止。

translations.literal: Local products were very scant; Chinese trading there carried only such things as porcelain and cooking pots -- at heaviest, nothing beyond cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The country had little to offer. Chinese merchants brought only porcelain, pots, and the like -- cloth was the weightiest cargo they could hope to sell.

sentences.zh: 後佛郎機據呂宋，多侵奪鄰境，惟二國號令不能及。

translations.literal: Later, when the Folangji held Luzon and greatly encroached on neighboring territories, only these two states lay beyond the reach of their orders.
translations.idiomatic: After the Portuguese seized Luzon and began annexing neighboring lands, only these two countries remained outside their control.

sentences.zh: 雞籠山在彭湖嶼東北，故名北港，又名東番，去泉州甚邇。

translations.literal: Chicken Cage Mountain lies northeast of the Pescadores, hence the name North Harbor; it is also called Eastern Barbarians, and is very close to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken Cage Mountain stood northeast of the Pescadores, whence the name North Harbor; it was also called Eastern Barbarians and lay very close to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 地多深山大澤，聚落星散。

translations.literal: The land had many deep mountains and great marshes, and settlements were scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Deep mountains and broad marshes covered the land, and villages were scattered far apart.

sentences.zh: 無君長，有十五社，社多者千人，少或五六百人。

translations.literal: There were no rulers; there were fifteen communities, the largest numbering a thousand persons, the smallest five or six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: There were no chiefs or kings, only fifteen communities of up to a thousand people each, some as small as five or six hundred.

sentences.zh: 無徭賦，以子女多者為雄，聽其號令。

translations.literal: There were no corvee or taxes; the man with the most children was regarded as foremost, and the people obeyed his commands.
translations.idiomatic: There was no taxation or forced labor. The man with the most children was treated as the leader, and others followed his word.

sentences.zh: 雖居海中，酷畏海，不善操舟，老死不與領國往來。

translations.literal: Although they lived amid the sea, they were intensely afraid of the sea and were not skilled at handling boats; until old age and death they had no dealings with neighboring countries.
translations.idiomatic: Though surrounded by sea, they were deeply afraid of it and poor sailors; most lived and died without ever visiting neighboring lands.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，鄭和遍歷東西洋，靡不獻琛恐後，獨東番遠避不至。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, Zheng He traversed the Eastern and Western Oceans; none failed to present tribute for fear of being late -- only the Eastern Barbarians kept far away and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign Zheng He toured the Eastern and Western Oceans, and every people rushed to offer tribute -- all except the Eastern Barbarians, who kept their distance and never appeared.

sentences.zh: 和惡之，家貽一銅鈴，俾掛諸項，蓋擬之狗國也。

translations.literal: He detested them and, to each household, bestowed a bronze bell to be hung at the neck, likening them to a dog country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He took offense and gave each household a bronze bell to hang around the neck, treating them like a nation of dogs.

sentences.zh: 其後，人反寶之，富者至掇數枚，曰：「此祖宗所遺。」

translations.literal: Afterward the people instead treasured them; the wealthy might collect several, saying: "These were left by our ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Later the people came to prize the bells instead; the wealthy collected several and said, "These were handed down by our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 俗尚勇，暇即習走，日可數百里，不讓奔馬。

translations.literal: The custom valued courage; in leisure they practiced running and could cover several hundred li in a day, not yielding to galloping horses.
translations.idiomatic: Bravery was honored, and in spare time men trained at running, covering several hundred li in a day -- a match for a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 足皮厚數分，履荊棘如平地。

translations.literal: The skin of the feet was several fen thick; they tread thorns and brambles as if on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: The soles of their feet were several fen thick, so they walked thorn and bramble as if on flat ground.

sentences.zh: 男女椎結，裸逐無所避。

translations.literal: Men and women wore topknots and ran naked without avoiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wore topknots and went naked in one another's presence without shame.

sentences.zh: 女或結草裙蔽體，遇長老則背身而立，俟過乃行。

translations.literal: Women sometimes tied grass skirts to cover the body; meeting elders they turned their backs and stood until they had passed, then went on.
translations.idiomatic: Women sometimes wore grass skirts for modesty. When they met an elder they turned away and waited until he had passed before moving on.

sentences.zh: 男子穿耳。

translations.literal: Men pierced their ears.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore pierced ears.

sentences.zh: 女子年十五，斷唇旁齒以為飾，手足皆刺文，眾社畢賀，費不貲。

translations.literal: When a girl reached fifteen, she broke the teeth beside her lips as ornament; hands and feet were all tattooed; every community congratulated her together, at expense beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen a girl had the teeth beside her lips knocked out for adornment and her hands and feet tattooed. The whole community turned out to celebrate, at staggering expense.

sentences.zh: 貧者不任受賀，則不敢刺。

translations.literal: The poor, unable to bear receiving congratulations, then did not dare to tattoo.
translations.idiomatic: Those too poor to host the celebration simply did without the tattoos.

sentences.zh: 四序，以草青為歲首。

translations.literal: Through the four seasons, they took the greening of the grass as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Their calendar began when the grass turned green.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀，而不善水田。

translations.literal: The soil suited the five grains, but they were not skilled at paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: The land supported grain crops, but the people did not practice wet-rice cultivation.

sentences.zh: 谷種落地，則止殺，謂行好事，助天公，乞飯食。

translations.literal: When grain seed fell to the ground, they then ceased killing, saying they were doing good deeds, helping the Lord of Heaven, and begging for food.
translations.idiomatic: Once seed was sown they stopped killing, declaring that they were doing good, aiding Heaven, and begging sustenance for the harvest.

sentences.zh: 既收穫，即標竹竿於道，謂之插青，此時逢外人便殺矣。

translations.literal: Once the harvest was in, they marked bamboo poles along the road -- called "inserting green" -- and at this time they killed any outsider they met.
translations.idiomatic: After the harvest they set up green-marked bamboo poles along the roads -- the "inserting green" season -- and killed any outsider they encountered.

sentences.zh: 村落相仇，刻期而後戰，勇者數人前跳，被殺則立散。

translations.literal: When villages bore grudges, they fixed a date and then fought; several brave men leaped forward first, and if one was killed the battle immediately dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Feuding villages set a day for battle. A few champions charged first; if one fell, the fight broke up at once.

sentences.zh: 其勝者，眾賀之，曰：「壯士能殺人也。」

translations.literal: The victors were congratulated by the crowd, who said: "The brave man can kill people."
translations.idiomatic: The victors were hailed with the words, "A brave man knows how to kill."

sentences.zh: 其負者，家眾亦賀之，曰：「壯士不畏死也。

translations.literal: The defeated side's families also congratulated them, saying: "The brave man does not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Even the losers' families offered praise: "A brave man does not fear death.

sentences.zh: 次日，即和好如初。

translations.literal: The next day they were reconciled as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the two sides were friends again.

sentences.zh: 地多竹，大至數拱，長十丈，以竹構屋，覆之以茅，廣且長，聚族而居。

translations.literal: The land had much bamboo, large enough to span several armfuls and ten zhang long; they built houses of bamboo, covered them with thatch, broad and long, and whole clans dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo grew there as thick as several arm-spans and ten zhang tall. Clans lived together in long, broad bamboo houses roofed with thatch.

sentences.zh: 無歷日、文字，有大事集眾議之。

translations.literal: They had no calendar days or writing; when great matters arose the multitude deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: They kept no calendar and had no writing; important decisions were settled in council.

sentences.zh: 善用鏢槍，竹柄鐵鏃，銛甚，試鹿鹿斃，試虎虎亦斃。

translations.literal: They were skilled with throwing spears -- bamboo shafts and iron points, very sharp: test them on a deer and the deer dies; test them on a tiger and the tiger dies too.
translations.idiomatic: They were expert with javelins -- bamboo shafts tipped with sharp iron points that would drop a deer on trial and a tiger as well.

sentences.zh: 性既畏海，捕魚則於溪澗。

translations.literal: Since by nature they feared the sea, they fished in streams and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid of the open sea by nature, they fished only in streams and creeks.

sentences.zh: 冬月聚眾捕鹿，鏢發輒中，積如丘山。

translations.literal: In the winter months they gathered in numbers to hunt deer; every cast of the javelin hit, and the pile rose like hills.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they hunted deer in parties; every throw found its mark, and the carcasses heaped up like hills.

sentences.zh: 獨不食雞雉，但取其毛以為飾。

translations.literal: They alone did not eat chickens or pheasants, but took only their feathers for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: They never ate chicken or pheasant, using only the feathers for decoration.

sentences.zh: 中多大溪，流入海，水澹，故其外名淡水洋。

translations.literal: Within the land were many great streams flowing into the sea; the water was fresh, hence the outer sea there was named the Freshwater Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Great rivers ran from the interior to the sea. Their water was fresh, and the adjoining waters were called the Freshwater Sea.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，倭寇擾閩，大將戚繼光敗之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiajing reign, Japanese pirates harassed Fujian; the great general Qi Jiguang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiajing reign Japanese pirates raided Fujian; the commander Qi Jiguang routed them.

sentences.zh: 倭遁居於此，其黨林道乾從之。

translations.literal: The Japanese fled and settled here, and their follower Lin Daoqian went with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese withdrew to this island, followed by the renegade Lin Daoqian.

sentences.zh: 已，道乾懼為倭所並，又懼官軍追擊，揚帆直抵浡泥，攘其邊地以居，號道乾港。

translations.literal: Before long, Daoqian feared being absorbed by the Japanese and also feared pursuit by government troops; he set sail straight for Brunei, seized border lands to dwell in, and called it Daoqian Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Daoqian, fearing annexation by the Japanese and pursuit by Ming forces, sailed to Brunei, carved out a strip of borderland, and established Daoqian Harbor.

sentences.zh: 而雞籠遭倭焚掠，國遂殘破。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Chicken Cage suffered burning and plunder by the Japanese, and the country was left broken and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Chicken Cage itself was burned and looted by the Japanese, and the settlements were left in ruins.

sentences.zh: 初悉居海濱，既遭倭難，稍稍避居山後。

translations.literal: At first they all lived on the seashore; after suffering Japanese troubles, they gradually moved to shelter behind the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They had first lived entirely on the coast; after the Japanese raids they gradually retreated inland behind the mountains.

sentences.zh: 忽中國漁舟從魍港飄至，遂往來通販，以為常。

translations.literal: Suddenly a Chinese fishing boat drifted in from Wanggang Harbor, and thereafter they came and went in trade until it became customary.
translations.idiomatic: Then a Chinese fishing boat blown in from Wanggang Harbor opened regular trade, which soon became routine.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆末，紅毛番泊舟於此，因事耕鑿，設阛阓，稱台灣焉。

translations.literal: By the end of the Wanli reign the Red-Haired foreigners anchored ships here, took up farming and building, established a marketplace, and called the place Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign the Dutch anchored there, cleared fields, built settlements, opened a market, and gave the place the name Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年，給事中何楷陳靖海之策，言：「自袁進、李忠、楊祿、楊策、鄭芝龍、李魁奇、鐘斌、劉香相繼為亂，海上歲無寧息。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen, the supervising secretary He Kai presented a plan to pacify the seas, saying: "Since Yuan Jin, Li Zhong, Yang Lu, Yang Ce, Zheng Zhilong, Li Kuiqi, Zhong Bin, and Liu Xiang rose in rebellion one after another, the seas have known no peace year after year.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 8 the supervising secretary He Kai submitted a plan to pacify the seas: "Since Yuan Jin, Li Zhong, Yang Lu, Yang Ce, Zheng Zhilong, Li Kuiqi, Zhong Bin, and Liu Xiang stirred rebellion in succession, the coast has not known a year of peace.

sentences.zh: 今欲靖寇氛，非墟其窟不可。

translations.literal: If one now wishes to still the bandit atmosphere, one cannot do so without destroying their lair.
translations.idiomatic: To end the piracy, their lair must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其窟維何？

translations.literal: What is their lair?
translations.idiomatic: Where is that lair?

sentences.zh: 台灣是也。

translations.literal: Taiwan is the place.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 台灣在彭湖島外，距漳、泉止兩日夜程，地廣而腴。

translations.literal: Taiwan lies outside the Pescadores, only two days and nights' journey from Zhang and Quan; the land is broad and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan lies beyond the Pescadores, only two days' sail from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, on broad and fertile ground.

sentences.zh: 初，貧民時至其地，規魚鹽之利，後見兵威不及，往往聚而為盜。

translations.literal: At first poor people occasionally went there to seek profit in fish and salt; later, seeing that military power did not reach them, they often gathered and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At first poor men went there for fish and salt; finding themselves beyond the reach of the law, many banded together as pirates.

sentences.zh: 近則紅毛築城其中，與奸民互市，屹然一大部落。

translations.literal: Recently the Red-Haired have built a fort there and trade with evil subjects, standing like a great settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Dutch have built a fort and trade with renegade Chinese, forming a substantial colony.

sentences.zh: 墟之之計，非可干戈從事，必嚴通海之禁，俾紅毛無從謀利，奸民無從得食，出兵四犯，我師乘其虛而擊之，可大得志。

translations.literal: The plan to destroy the lair cannot rely on force of arms; one must strictly forbid sea traffic, so that the Red-Haired have no way to seek profit and evil subjects no way to obtain food; then send troops to raid on four fronts, and our army can strike when they are weakened and achieve great success.
translations.idiomatic: Destroying this nest cannot be done by force alone. Seal off sea trade so the Dutch cannot profit and outlaws cannot eat; then raid on four fronts and strike when they are weakened -- that is how to succeed.

sentences.zh: 紅毛舍此而去，然後海氛可靖也。」

translations.literal: Once the Red-Haired abandon the place and leave, only then can the sea atmosphere be stilled."
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Dutch abandon Taiwan will the seas be calm again."

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time his advice was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not act on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 其地，北自雞籠，南至浪嶠，可一千餘里。

translations.literal: The territory, from Chicken Cage in the north to Langjiao in the south, was about a thousand-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: The island stretched some thirteen hundred li from Chicken Cage in the north to Langjiao in the south.

sentences.zh: 東自多羅滿，西至王城，可九百餘裡。

translations.literal: From Duoluoman in the east to Wangcheng in the west, it was about nine hundred-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: From Duoluoman in the east to Wangcheng in the west, it measured roughly nine hundred li.

sentences.zh: 水道，順風，自雞籠淡水至福州港口。

translations.literal: By water, with a fair wind, from Chicken Cage Freshwater to Fuzhou harbor.
translations.idiomatic: By sea, with a fair wind, from Chicken Cage Freshwater to Fuzhou harbor:

sentences.zh: 五更可達。

translations.literal: Five watches will suffice to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: five watches.

sentences.zh: 自台灣港至彭湖嶼，四更可達。

translations.literal: From Taiwan harbor to the Pescadores, four watches will suffice to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From Taiwan harbor to the Pescadores: four watches.

sentences.zh: 自彭湖至金門，七更可達。

translations.literal: From the Pescadores to Kinmen, seven watches will suffice to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: From the Pescadores to Kinmen: seven watches.

sentences.zh: 東北至日本，七十更可達。

translations.literal: Northeast to Japan, seventy watches will suffice to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast to Japan: seventy watches.

sentences.zh: 南至呂宋，六十更可達。

translations.literal: South to Luzon, sixty watches will suffice to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: South to Luzon: sixty watches.

sentences.zh: 蓋海道不可以裡計，舟人分一晝夜為十更，故以更計道里雲。

translations.literal: For sea routes cannot be reckoned in li; sailors divide one day and night into ten watches, hence distances at sea are counted in watches, as said.
translations.idiomatic: Sea distances cannot be measured in li. Mariners divide day and night into ten watches, and so reckon voyages in watches rather than miles.

sentences.zh: 婆羅，又名文萊，東洋盡處，西洋所自起也。

translations.literal: Borneo, also called Brunei, is where the Eastern Ocean ends and the Western Ocean begins.
translations.idiomatic: Borneo, also known as Brunei, marked the eastern limit of the Eastern Ocean and the beginning of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 唐時有婆羅國，高宗時常入貢。

translations.literal: In Tang times there was a Borneo state; in the Gaozong reign it often sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tang records mention a Borneo kingdom that regularly sent tribute during the reign of Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年十月遣使者齎璽書、彩幣撫諭其王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yongle, envoys were dispatched bearing imperial letters and colored silks to comfort and instruct its king.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 3 the court sent envoys with imperial letters and silks to confer with its king.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，其國東、西二王並遣使奉表朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the eastern and western kings of the state both sent envoys to present memorials and tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yongle 4 both the eastern and western kings sent envoys with memorials and tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年又貢。

translations.literal: The next year they sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again the following year.

sentences.zh: 其地負山面海，崇釋教，惡殺喜施。

translations.literal: The land backed onto mountains and faced the sea; they revered Buddhism, hated killing, and delighted in giving.
translations.idiomatic: Mountainous and sea-girt, the country followed Buddhism, abhorred killing, and favored charity.

sentences.zh: 禁食豕肉，犯者罪死。

translations.literal: They forbade eating pork; offenders were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Pork was forbidden on pain of death.

sentences.zh: 王薙發，裹金繡巾，佩雙劍，出入徒步，從者二百餘人。

translations.literal: The king shaved his head, wrapped a gold-embroidered turban, wore two swords at his belt, went on foot when entering or leaving, and was followed by more than two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: The king shaved his head, wore a gold-embroidered turban and two swords at his belt, walked wherever he went, and was attended by more than two hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 有禮拜寺，每祭用犧。

translations.literal: There were mosques; at each sacrifice they used sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: There were houses of worship where sacrifices were offered with livestock.

sentences.zh: 厥貢玳瑁、瑪瑙、硨磲、珠、白焦布、花焦布、降真香、黃蠟、黑小廝。

translations.literal: Their tribute comprised tortoiseshell, agate, giant-clam shell, pearls, plain gauze cloth, patterned gauze cloth, eaglewood, yellow wax, and black boys.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included tortoiseshell, agate, giant-clam shell, pearls, plain and patterned gauze, eaglewood, yellow beeswax, and black servants.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，為王者閩人也。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign the one who ruled was a man of Min.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wanli reign the throne was held by a man from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 或言鄭和使婆羅，有閩人從之，因留居其地，其後人竟據其國而王之。

translations.literal: Some say that when Zheng He went as envoy to Borneo, a man of Min followed him and remained to dwell there; his descendants ultimately seized the country and became its kings.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when Zheng He visited Borneo a Fujianese man in his party stayed behind, and his descendants eventually seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 邸旁有中國碑。

translations.literal: Beside the royal residence was a Chinese stele.
translations.idiomatic: A Chinese stele stood beside the royal residence.

sentences.zh: 王有金印一，篆文，上作獸形，言永樂朝所賜。

translations.literal: The king had one gold seal, in seal script, topped with an animal form; it was said to have been bestowed in the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: The king possessed a gold seal in seal script surmounted by an animal figure, said to have been granted in the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 民間嫁娶，必請此印印背上，以為榮。

translations.literal: For weddings among the people, they always asked to have this seal stamped on the back as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At weddings commoners sought the honor of having this seal impressed on the bride's back.

sentences.zh: 後佛郎機橫，舉兵來擊。

translations.literal: Later the Folangji ran rampant and raised troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Portuguese grew aggressive and marched against the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王率國人走入山谷中，放藥水，流出，毒殺其人無算，王得返國。

translations.literal: The king led his people into the mountain valleys, released poisoned water that flowed out, and poisoned their men beyond counting; the king was able to return to his country.
translations.idiomatic: The king withdrew with his people into the hills and released poisoned water downstream, killing countless Portuguese; he then recovered his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機遂犯呂宋。

translations.literal: The Folangji then invaded Luzon.
translations.idiomatic: The Portuguese then turned their attack on Luzon.

sentences.zh: 麻葉甕

translations.literal: Belitung Island
translations.idiomatic: Belitung Island

sentences.zh: 麻葉甕，在西南海中。

translations.literal: Mayeuwong lies in the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Mayeuwong lay in the southwestern sea.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年十月遣使齎璽書賜物，招諭其國，迄不朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yongle, envoys were sent bearing the imperial seal and letter and bestowing goods to summon and instruct the state; to the end it never came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle 3 the court sent envoys with an imperial letter and gifts to summon and reassure the kingdom, but it never sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 自佔城靈山放舟，順風十晝夜至交欄山，其西南即麻葉甕。

translations.literal: Setting sail from Lingshan in Champa, with a favorable wind one reached Jiaolan Mountain in ten days and nights; southwest of it is Mayeuwong.
translations.idiomatic: From Lingshan in Champa, a fair wind carried a ship ten days and nights to Jiaolan Mountain; Mayeuwong lay to its southwest.

sentences.zh: 山峻地平，田膏腴，收獲倍他國。

translations.literal: The mountains are steep and the land level; the fields are rich and fertile, and harvests double those of other states.
translations.idiomatic: Steep mountains rose above level ground, the soil was rich, and harvests ran to twice those of neighboring lands.

sentences.zh: 煮海為鹽，釀蔗為酒。

translations.literal: They boil the sea for salt and ferment sugarcane for wine.
translations.idiomatic: They boiled seawater for salt and fermented sugarcane into wine.

sentences.zh: 男女椎結，衣長衫，圍之以布。

translations.literal: Men and women wear topknots, long gowns, and wrap cloth around themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wore topknots and long gowns, with cloth wrapped about them.

sentences.zh: 俗尚節義，婦喪夫，剺面剃髮，絕粒七日，與屍同寢，多死。

translations.literal: The custom honors chastity and righteousness; when a wife loses her husband she lacerates her face, shaves her head, abstains from grain for seven days, and sleeps beside the corpse--many die.
translations.idiomatic: The people prized fidelity: when a woman lost her husband she scarred her face, shaved her head, ate nothing for seven days, and slept beside the corpse--and many died.

sentences.zh: 七日不死，則親戚勸以飲食，終身不再嫁。

translations.literal: If she does not die within seven days, relatives then persuade her with food and drink, and she never remarries for life.
translations.idiomatic: If she survived the seven days, kin would coax her to eat; she then remained a widow for life.

sentences.zh: 或於焚屍日，亦赴火自焚。

translations.literal: Some, on the day the corpse is burned, also throw themselves into the fire and burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some women, on the day the body was cremated, threw themselves into the flames as well.

sentences.zh: 產玳瑁、木棉、黃蠟、檳榔、花布之屬。

translations.literal: It produces tortoiseshell, cotton, yellow wax, betel nut, patterned cloth, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included tortoiseshell, cotton, yellow beeswax, betel nuts, and patterned cloth.

sentences.zh: 交欄山甚高廣，饒竹木。

translations.literal: Jiaolan Mountain is very high and broad, abundant in bamboo and timber.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaolan Mountain was lofty and wide, rich in bamboo and timber.

sentences.zh: 元史弼、高興伐爪哇，遭風至此山下，舟多壞，乃登山伐木重造，遂破爪哇。

translations.literal: When Shi Bi and Gao Xing of the Yuan invaded Java, they were blown by wind to the foot of this mountain; many boats were wrecked, so they climbed the mountain to fell timber and rebuild, and thereafter broke Java.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan generals Shi Bi and Gao Xing invaded Java, a storm drove them to this mountain; many ships were wrecked, so they climbed it to cut timber, rebuilt their fleet, and went on to conquer Java.

sentences.zh: 其病卒百餘，留養不歸，後益蕃衍，故其地多華人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred of their sick soldiers were left behind to convalesce and did not return; they later multiplied ever more, so the place has many Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred sick soldiers were left behind to recover and never went home; their numbers grew, and the region came to have a large Chinese population.

sentences.zh: 又有葛卜及速兒米囊二國，亦永樂三年遣使持璽書賜物招諭，竟不至。

translations.literal: There were also the two states of Gebu and Su'erminang; in the third year of Yongle envoys were likewise sent bearing the imperial seal and letter and gifts to summon and instruct them, but in the end they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby were Gebu and Su'erminang; in Yongle 3 the court likewise sent envoys with an imperial letter and gifts to summon them, but they never came.

sentences.zh: 古麻剌朗

translations.literal: Gumalalang
translations.idiomatic: Gumalalang

sentences.zh: 古麻剌朗，東南海中小國也。

translations.literal: Gumalalang is also a small state in the southeastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Gumalalang was another small kingdom in the southeastern sea.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年九月遣中官張謙齎敕撫諭其王干剌義亦奔敦，賜之絨錦、纟寧絲、紗羅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Yongle, the eunuch Zhang Qian was sent bearing an edict to comfort and instruct the king Ganlayi Yibendun, bestowing on him velvet brocade, ramie silk, and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongle 15 the eunuch Zhang Qian was sent with an edict to reassure King Ganlayi Yibendun, granting him velvet brocade, ramie silk, and gauze.

sentences.zh: 十八年八月，王率妻子、陪臣隨謙來朝，貢方物，禮之如蘇祿國王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year, the king led his wife, children, and attending ministers to follow Qian to court, presenting local products; he was treated like the king of Sulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year the king brought his wife, children, and ministers to court with Zhang Qian, bearing tribute; he was received with the same honors as the king of Sulu.

sentences.zh: 王言：「臣愚無知，雖為國人所推，然未受朝命，幸賜封誥，仍其國號。」

translations.literal: The king said: "Your subject is foolish and ignorant; though pushed forward by the people of the state, I have not received the court's command-- I beg to be granted an investiture patent, keeping the state's name."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "Your subject is foolish and knows nothing. Though my people have pressed me forward, I have never received appointment from the court. I beg that you grant me an investiture patent and let my kingdom keep its name."

sentences.zh: 從之，乃賜以印誥、冠帶、儀仗、鞍馬及文綺、金織襲衣，妃以下並有賜。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and he was bestowed a seal patent, cap and belt, ceremonial regalia, saddle and horse, and figured silks and gold-woven ceremonial robes; the consort and those below all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and granted him a seal patent, cap and belt, ceremonial regalia, saddle and horse, figured silks, and gold-woven state robes; his consort and the rest of his party received gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 明年正月辭還，復賜金銀錢、文綺、紗羅、彩帛、金織襲衣、麒麟衣，妃以下賜有差。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he took leave to return, and was again given gold, silver, cash, figured silks, gauzes, colored silks, gold-woven ceremonial robes, and qilin robes; gifts to the consort and those below were graded.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month he took leave to return home and received further gifts of gold, silver, cash, figured silks, gauzes, colored silks, gold-woven state robes, and qilin robes; the consort and her attendants were rewarded in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 王還至福建，遘疾卒。

translations.literal: When the king returned as far as Fujian, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey home the king fell ill in Fujian and died.

sentences.zh: 遣禮部主事楊善諭祭，謚曰康靖，有司治墳，葬以王禮。

translations.literal: Yang Shan, a principal secretary of the Ministry of Rites, was sent to perform the condolence sacrifice; he was given the posthumous title Kangjing, officials prepared the tomb, and he was buried with royal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shan, a principal secretary of the Ministry of Rites, was sent to offer condolence sacrifices; the court posthumously titled him Kangjing, local officials prepared his tomb, and he was buried with royal honors.

sentences.zh: 命其子剌苾嗣為王，率眾歸，賜鈔幣。

translations.literal: His son Labi was ordered to succeed as king, led the people home, and was granted paper money.
translations.idiomatic: His son Labi was appointed to succeed him, led the party home, and was granted paper money.

sentences.zh: 馮嘉施蘭

translations.literal: Pangasinan
translations.idiomatic: Pangasinan

sentences.zh: 馮嘉施蘭，亦東洋中小國。

translations.literal: Pangasinan is also a small state of the Eastern Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Pangasinan was likewise a small state of the Eastern Ocean.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年八月，其酋嘉馬銀等來朝，貢方物，賜鈔幣有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Yongle, its chieftain Jiamayin and others came to court, presenting local products; paper money was granted in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongle 4 its chieftain Jiamayin and others came to court with tribute and received graded gifts of paper money.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，其酋玳瑁、裡欲二人，各率其屬朝貢，賜二人鈔各百錠、文綺六表裡，其從者亦有賜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, its chieftains Daimao and Liyu, each leading their followers, came to court with tribute; each man was granted a hundred ingots of paper money and six suits of figured silk with lining, and their attendants also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year its chieftains Daimao and Liyu each brought their followers to court; each received a hundred ingots of paper money and six lined suits of figured silk, and their attendants were rewarded as well.

sentences.zh: 八年復來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they came again with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 文郎馬神

translations.literal: Banjarmasin
translations.idiomatic: Banjarmasin

sentences.zh: 文郎馬神，以木為城，其半倚山。

translations.literal: Banjarmasin has a wooden palisade for a city, half of it leaning against a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Banjarmasin was walled in timber, half the settlement built against a mountainside.

sentences.zh: 酋蓄繡女數百人。

translations.literal: The chieftain keeps several hundred embroidered maidens.
translations.idiomatic: Its ruler kept several hundred embroidered maidens in attendance.

sentences.zh: 出乘象，則繡女執衣履、刀劍及檳榔盤以從。

translations.literal: When he goes out riding an elephant, the embroidered maidens carry clothes, shoes, swords, and betel trays and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad on an elephant, the maidens followed bearing clothes, shoes, swords, and betel trays.

sentences.zh: 或泛舟，則酋趺坐床上，繡女列坐其下，與相向，或用以刺舟，威儀甚都。

translations.literal: Sometimes when boating, the chieftain sits cross-legged on a bed while the embroidered maidens sit in rows below, facing him; some use oars to propel the boat--the display of authority is most imposing.
translations.idiomatic: On the water he sat cross-legged on a couch while the maidens sat in rows below, facing him; some poled the boat. The spectacle was stately in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 民多縛木水上，築室以居，如三佛齊。

translations.literal: The people mostly bind logs on the water and build dwellings to live in, as in Srivijaya.
translations.idiomatic: Most people lashed logs together on the water and built houses to live in, as in Srivijaya.

sentences.zh: 男女用五色布纏頭，腹背多袒，或著小袖衣，蒙頭而入，下體圍以幔。

translations.literal: Men and women wrap their heads in cloth of five colors; chest and back are mostly bare, or they wear short-sleeved jackets, entering with veiled heads and lower bodies wrapped in skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wound their heads in cloth of five colors, baring chest and back, or wore short-sleeved jackets with veiled heads and skirts about the lower body.

sentences.zh: 初用蕉葉為食器，後與華人市，漸用磁器。

translations.literal: At first they used banana leaves as food vessels; later they traded with Chinese and gradually came to use porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: They once ate from banana leaves; trade with Chinese merchants gradually brought them to porcelain.

sentences.zh: 尤好磁甕，畫龍其外，死則貯甕中以葬。

translations.literal: They especially favor porcelain jars painted with dragons on the outside; when one dies the body is stored in a jar for burial.
translations.idiomatic: They prized porcelain jars painted with dragons on the outside; the dead were placed in such jars for burial.

sentences.zh: 其俗惡淫，奸者論死。

translations.literal: Their custom abhors licentiousness; adulterers are sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The people abhorred licentiousness, and adultery was punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 華人與女通，輒削其發，以女配之，永不聽歸。

translations.literal: If a Chinese man lies with a woman, his hair is shaved off and the woman is given to him in marriage; he is never allowed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: If a Chinese man slept with a local woman, his head was shaved and the woman given to him in marriage; he was never allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 女苦發短，問華人何以致長，紿之曰：「我用華水沐之，故長耳。」

translations.literal: Women, troubled by short hair, asked Chinese men how to make it grow long; they were deceived, saying: "I wash it with Chinese water, and so it grows long."
translations.idiomatic: The women, vexed by their short hair, asked Chinese men how to make it grow; the men lied, "I wash mine in Chinese water, and that is why it is long."

sentences.zh: 其女信之，競市船中水以沐。

translations.literal: The women believed this and competed to buy water from the ships to wash their hair.
translations.idiomatic: The women believed them and vied to buy water from the ships to wash their hair.

sentences.zh: 華人故靳之，以為笑端。

translations.literal: The Chinese deliberately withheld it, making it a source of amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese deliberately rationed the water and laughed at them.

sentences.zh: 女或悅華人，持香蕉、甘蔗、茉莉相贈遺，多與之調笑。

translations.literal: Some women, taking a liking to Chinese men, would offer bananas, sugarcane, and jasmine back and forth, often flirting with them.
translations.idiomatic: Some women who took a fancy to Chinese men would bring them bananas, sugarcane, and jasmine, bantering and flirting as they came and went.

sentences.zh: 然憚其法嚴，無敢私通者。

translations.literal: Yet they feared the strictness of the law, and none dared secret liaisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the law was strict, and none dared a secret affair.

sentences.zh: 其深山中有村名烏籠裡憚，其人盡生尾，見人輒掩面走避。

translations.literal: Deep in the mountains there is a village called Wulonglidan; its people are all born with tails, and at the sight of others they cover their faces and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the mountains was a village called Wulonglidan whose people were born with tails; at the sight of strangers they covered their faces and fled.

sentences.zh: 然地饒沙金，商人持貨往市者，擊小銅鼓為號，置貨地上，即引退丈許。

translations.literal: Yet the land is rich in placer gold; when merchants bring goods to trade, they beat a small copper drum as a signal, set the goods on the ground, and withdraw about a zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The country was rich in placer gold all the same. Merchants who came to trade beat a small copper drum, set their goods on the ground, and withdrew a few paces.

sentences.zh: 其人乃前視，當意者，置金於旁。

translations.literal: The villagers then come forward to inspect; if satisfied, they place gold beside the goods.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers came forward to look; if pleased, they laid gold beside the goods.

sentences.zh: 主者遙語欲售，則持貨去，否則懷金以歸，不交言也。

translations.literal: If the owner calls from afar that he wishes to sell, they take the goods; if not, they carry the gold back--no words are exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: If the merchant shouted from a distance that he would sell, they took the goods; if not, they carried the gold away. Not a word passed between them.

sentences.zh: 所產有犀牛、孔雀、鸚鵡、沙金、鶴頂、降香、蠟、藤席、惸藤、蓽撥、血竭、肉荳蔻、麞皮諸物。

translations.literal: Local products include rhinoceros, peacocks, parrots, placer gold, hornbill casques, aloeswood, wax, rattan mats, rattan, long pepper, dragon's blood, nutmeg, and deer hides.
translations.idiomatic: Products included rhinoceros horn, peacocks, parrots, placer gold, hornbill casques, aloeswood, wax, rattan mats, rattan, long pepper, dragon's blood resin, nutmeg, and deerskin.

sentences.zh: 鄰境有買哇柔者，性凶狠，每夜半盜斬人頭以去，裝之以金。

translations.literal: In a neighboring region are the Maiwarou, fierce and cruel; each midnight they steal in and behead people, fitting the heads with gold.
translations.idiomatic: In a neighboring land lived the Maiwarou, a fierce people who at midnight would steal in, cut off a head, and adorn it with gold.

sentences.zh: 故商人畏之，夜必嚴更以待。

translations.literal: Merchants therefore fear them and must keep strict night watches.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants feared them and kept strict night watches.

sentences.zh: 始，文郎馬神酋有賢德，待商人以恩信。

translations.literal: At first the chieftain of Banjarmasin had virtue and treated merchants with kindness and trust.
translations.idiomatic: At first Banjarmasin's ruler was a man of virtue who treated merchants with kindness and good faith.

sentences.zh: 子三十一人，恐擾商舶，不令外出。

translations.literal: He had thirty-one sons; fearing they would harass merchant ships, he did not allow them to go abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirty-one sons, but fearing they would trouble merchant ships, he forbade them to go abroad.

sentences.zh: 其妻乃買哇柔酋長之妹，生子襲父位，聽其母族之言，務為欺詐，多負商人價直，自是赴者亦稀。

translations.literal: His wife was the sister of the Maiwarou chieftain; their son succeeded to his father's place, heeded his mother's clan, and devoted himself to fraud, often defaulting on what he owed merchants--after that those who came grew scarce.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the sister of the Maiwarou chieftain. Their son succeeded him, listened to his mother's kin, and turned to deceit, often cheating merchants of their due; from then on fewer traders came.
